data.title: Quantum mechanics provide truly random numbers on demand
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）利用量子力学原理开发的真正随机数生成器。传统算法只能生成伪随机数，而量子力学由于其内在的随机性，可以生成无法预测的真正随机数。NIST通过贝尔测试实验，利用纠缠光子的特性，确保了随机数的真实性和可验证性。他们与科罗拉多大学博尔德分校合作，创建了“科罗拉多大学随机信标”（CURBy），每日自动生成并发布随机数，供公众使用。这是首个利用量子非定域性生成随机数的服务，具有高度透明性和可验证性，是随机数生成技术的一大里程碑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：随机性和量子随机数生成器的性质及其应用

不同观点：
• **模拟宇宙论与随机性**：moktonar认为我们生活在一个模拟中，随机值由外部产生，对于我们来说是"真正随机"的，因为无法得知种子值。这种观点强调了我们无法完美模拟宇宙或预测未来，因为数学模型无法产生真正的随机数。
   
• **硬件随机数生成器的使用**：vayup指出，当前行业广泛使用硬件随机数生成器，其熵值来源于物理现象，且熵源的不足并不是问题。这表明实际应用中，通过物理手段获取的随机数已足够使用。

• **在线随机数服务的可靠性**：btilly提到像random.org这样的服务在公开验证随机数方面足够可靠，但大多数加密应用并不需要公开可验证的随机数。

• **随机性的本质与量子力学**：mathattack和perching_aix讨论了是否存在真正的随机性。mathattack引述教授的观点，认为量子层面的随机性是可能的。perching_aix进一步探讨了我们如何识别真正的随机性，以及是否可能存在未知的变量影响测量结果。

• **量子随机性与测量**：ang_cire关注量子随机性是否真正随机，提出测量过程中可能存在未被考虑的变量，并以量子纠缠实验为例进行讨论。

• **随机数在加密中的应用**：JKCalhoun和t_mann讨论了随机数在加密中的应用，包括创建一对一次性密码本和将公开随机数转换为私有随机数的风险。

• **硬件随机数生成器的实际问题**：EastLondonCoder分享了在博彩行业中硬件随机数生成器失败的实际案例，强调了设备过热导致的问题。

• **随机性的定义与算法预测**：gregfjohnson和jmyeet从算法和复杂性角度讨论了随机性的定义，提出是否存在可以预测量子随机性的算法，以及通过Kolmogorov复杂性来理解随机性。

补充讨论：
• **对随机数生成器的实际需求和问题**：讨论中涉及到随机数生成器在不同领域（如加密、博彩）的实际需求和问题，强调了硬件和量子随机数生成器的应用场景和局限性。

• **对量子随机性的哲学探讨**：一些评论者对量子随机性是否真正随机进行了哲学探讨，质疑我们是否能够识别和证明真正的随机性，或者只是由于我们知识的局限性导致某些现象看似随机。

总体而言，讨论围绕随机性的本质、量子力学在随机性中的角色、以及随机数在实际应用中的可靠性和安全性展开。争议的焦点主要在于量子随机性是否真正随机，以及我们如何定义和验证随机性。

The GIST
Quantum mechanics provide truly random numbers on demand
by
National Institute of Standards and Technology
edited by
Sadie Harley
, 																								reviewed by
Robert Egan
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
peer-reviewed publication
trusted source
proofread
Instrumentation for the quantum random number generator in the NIST Boulder laboratories. Credit: NIST
Randomness is incredibly useful. People often draw straws, throw dice or flip coins to make fair choices. Random numbers can enable auditors to make completely unbiased selections. Randomness is also key in security; if a password or code is an unguessable string of numbers, it's harder to crack. Many of our cryptographic systems today use random number generators to produce secure keys.
But how do you know that a random number is truly random?
Classical computer algorithms can only create pseudorandom numbers, and someone with enough knowledge of the algorithm or the system could manipulate it or predict the next number. An expert in sleight of hand could rig a coin flip to guarantee a heads or tails result. Even the most careful coin flips can have bias; with enough study, their outcomes could be predicted.
"True
randomness
is something that nothing in the universe can predict in advance," said Krister Shalm, a physicist at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Even if a random number generator used seemingly random processes in nature, it would be hard to verify that those numbers are truly random, Shalm added.
Einstein believed that nature isn't random, famously saying, "God does not play dice with the universe." Scientists have since proved that Einstein was wrong.
Unlike dice or computer algorithms,
quantum mechanics
is inherently random. Carrying out a quantum experiment called a Bell test, Shalm and his team have transformed this source of true quantum randomness into a traceable and certifiable random-number service.
"If God does play dice with the universe, then you can turn that into the best random number generator that the universe allows," Shalm said. "We really wanted to take that experiment out of the lab and turn it into a useful public service."
To make that happen, NIST researchers and their colleagues at the University of Colorado Boulder created the Colorado University Randomness Beacon (
CURBy
). CURBy produces
random numbers
automatically and broadcasts them daily through a website for anyone to use. The related research is
published
in the journal
Nature
.
At the heart of this service is the NIST-run Bell test, which provides truly random results. This randomness acts as a kind of raw material that the rest of the researchers' setup "refines" into random numbers published by the beacon.
The Bell test measures pairs of "entangled" photons whose properties are correlated even when separated by vast distances. When researchers measure an individual particle, the outcome is random, but the properties of the pair are more correlated than
classical physics
allows, enabling researchers to verify the randomness. Einstein called this quantum nonlocality "spooky action at a distance."
This is the first random number generator service to use quantum nonlocality as a source of its numbers, and the most transparent source of random numbers to date. That's because the results are certifiable and traceable to a greater extent than ever before.

"CURBy is one of the first publicly available services that operates with a provable quantum advantage. That's a big milestone for us," Shalm explained. "The quality and origin of these random bits can be directly certified in a way that conventional
random number generators
are unable to."
From left to right, Jasper Palfree University of Colorado Boulder), Gautam Kavuri (NIST) and Krister Shalm (NIST). Credit: NIST
NIST performed one of the first complete experimental Bell tests in 2015, which firmly established that
quantum mechanics is truly random
. In 2018, NIST pioneered methods to use these Bell tests to build
the world's first sources of true randomness.
However, turning these quantum correlations into random numbers is hard work. NIST's first breakthrough demonstrations of the Bell test required months of setup to run for a few hours, and it took a great deal of time to collect enough data to generate 512 bits of true randomness.

data.title: GitHub CI/CD observability with OpenTelemetry step by step guide
data.author: ankit01-oss
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了如何使用OpenTelemetry为GitHub Actions的CI/CD管道增加可观察性。OpenTelemetry是一个开源的可观察性框架，能够以标准、供应商无关的方式收集 traces、metrics 和 logs。文章解释了为何要使用 OpenTelemetry 观察 CI/CD 管道，包括实现端到端可见性、性能优化、错误检测与调试，以及依赖分析等优势。通过配置 OpenTelemetry Collector 和 GitHub Receiver，可以捕获工作流事件作为 traces，并通过 GitHub API 获取 metrics。文章还提供了具体的设置步骤，包括配置 GitHub 网络钩子和访问令牌，以实现对 GitHub Actions 的全面监控。

主要讨论点：开源可观察性工具（如Prometheus、OpenTelemetry）与商业工具（如DataDog、CloudWatch、Sentry）的比较和使用体验，特别是在不同基础设施和应用场景下的适用性。

不同观点：
• **Prometheus + OpenTelemetry + Grafana组合的优点**：
   - [drzaiusx11] 认为Prometheus + OpenTelemetry (OTel) + Grafana组合非常易用，能够轻松添加新的报警和仪表板，且不怀念DataDog。
   - 强调了开源工具在自建基础设施下的灵活性和易用性。

• **OTel在批处理和异步任务中的使用**：
   - [hrpnk] 对OTel在长时间运行的批处理和异步任务中的表现提出疑问，特别是与单体应用的对比，关注其适用性和性能。

• **CloudWatch vs. 自建基础设施的可观察性工具**：
   - [reactordev] 认为像SigNoz、Prometheus等开源工具只能基于暴露的数据工作，而CloudWatch因为拥有更多底层数据，在AWS环境下表现更优。
   - 但同时指出，如果拥有自建基础设施，SigNoz是更好的选择，且一旦选择了OTel，切换路径会非常痛苦。

   - [candiddevmike] 询问SigNoz与其他“一体化”OTel平台的比较，特别是其开源部分和付费功能之间的区别。

补充讨论：

   - [127dot1] 认为文章标题误导，内容仅限于GitHub CI/CD，不具有普遍性。

争议焦点：
• 开源可观察性工具（如OTel、Prometheus、SigNoz）与商业工具（如DataDog、CloudWatch、Sentry）的选择和集成复杂性。
• OTel在特定场景（如批处理、异步任务、GitHub Actions）中的适用性和实现方式。
• 供应商锁定问题与工具切换的痛苦。

Part of OpenTelemetry Track
openTelemetry
June 10, 2025

9 min read
CI/CD Observability with OpenTelemetry - A Step by Step Guide
Author:
Elizabeth Mathew
In the fast-paced world of CI/CD, understanding the performance and behaviour of your pipelines is crucial. GitHub Actions has become a popular choice for automating builds and deployments, but anyone who's debugged a flaky workflow or long-running job knows how challenging it can be to get visibility into what's happening under the hood. We usually rely on build logs, timing data, or guesswork when something goes wrong.
Wouldn't it be nice to trace a pipeline run step-by-step, or have metrics on how your workflows are performing over time?
This is where OpenTelemetry comes into play.
OpenTelemetry [OTel]
is an open-source observability framework that enables collecting traces, metrics, and logs in a standard, vendor-agnostic way. With a bit of configuration, OTel can capture telemetry from even our CI/CD pipelines. In this guide, we'll walk through setting up OpenTelemetry for GitHub Actions [covering both tracing and metrics], with practical examples and configuration snippets.
Why Observe CI/CD Pipelines with OpenTelemetry [OTel]?
Just as we use traces and metrics to understand microservices and applications, we can apply the same to CI/CD pipelines. Instrumenting GitHub Actions with OpenTelemetry yields several benefits:
End-to-end visibility:
You can trace the entire lifecycle of a workflow run, from trigger to completion. Each job and step can be visualised, showing how they execute and interact.
Performance optimisation:
By measuring the duration of each job and step, you can identify bottlenecks or slow steps in your pipeline.
For example, a long testing phase or a slow dependency installation.
Error detection and debugging:
Traces can pinpoint exactly where a workflow failed or took an unexpected path, making it easier to debug broken pipelines. Instead of combing through logs, you'll see which step or action resulted in an error.
Dependency analysis:
In complex workflows with multiple jobs [possibly with dependencies or concurrent runs], tracing helps you understand how different jobs and steps relate to each other within the workflow.
Traditionally, engineering teams have monitored CI pipelines using ad-hoc methods, maybe exporting build logs to an ELK stack, timing data to Prometheus, or using CI-specific analytics. Those approaches often cover only metrics [like durations, success/failure counts] or logs. OpenTelemetry provides a unified approach, it can capture
traces
[for structure and timing] and
metrics
[for quantitative monitoring] in one system.
Every pipeline run can become a trace, and important KPIs can be emitted as metrics using OTel. Next, we'll see how to set this up with GitHub Actions.
How OpenTelemetry Captures GitHub Actions Data
To make GitHub Actions observable with OTel, we leverage a component of the OTel Collector known as the
GitHub Receiver
. This receiver can do some very cool things like,
Ingest GitHub workflow events as traces:
GitHub can send events [via webhooks] whenever workflows run or jobs execute. The GitHub Receiver accepts these events and converts them into trace data.
Scrape GitHub metrics via the API:
The same receiver can use GitHub's APIs [GraphQL and REST] to scrape repository and workflow-related metrics. This includes information like
repository size, star count, open pull requests, issue counts, contributor statistics
, and more.
📝
Note
We can set intervals at which scraping should take place when configuring the receiver as shown below:
github
:
initial_delay
:
1s
collection_interval
:
60s
In the sections below, we'll go through the steps to configure the OpenTelemetry Collector with the GitHub receiver for both traces and metrics.
Setting Up the OpenTelemetry Collector for GitHub Actions Observability
Okay. Let's dive into the setup.
Step 0: Updating Your GitHub Config
On the GitHub side of things, you'll need to set up a webhook on your repository [or organization] that sends
workflow_run
and
workflow_job
events to your Collector endpoint. In GitHub's settings, add a new webhook and select at least these two event types, with the content type set to
application/json
.
We will configure the Collector to listen for these events on a specific URL. You'll also need a secret token for the webhook [a random string] to secure it; the Collector will use the same secret to validate incoming events.
For metrics, if you want to scrape data from the GitHub API, you'll need an access token with permissions to read repo and workflow data. You can read this
guide
to understand how to get your personal access token.
Configure your GitHub webhook
With that in place, let's set up the Collector step by step.
Step 1: Install/ Update the OTel Collector
If you haven't already, install the OpenTelemetry Collector [we'll use the
otelcol-contrib
distribution because the GitHub receiver is part of the contrib components

data.title: Transparent peer review to be extended to all of Nature's research papers
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 自2020年以来，《Nature》期刊允许作者选择将同行评审文件与论文一同发表。从2025年6月16日起，所有新提交并发表为研究文章的手稿将自动包含评审报告和作者回应的链接，评审者身份保持匿名，除非他们选择公开。此举旨在增加科学过程的透明度，揭示论文形成的细节，增强公众对科学的信任。通过公开评审报告，可以让更多人了解科学讨论的过程，特别是对早期研究人员有重要价值。科学知识随着新证据的出现而演变，而同行评审是提升论文质量的关键部分，应该被视为科学记录的重要组成部分。此举也是对科研评价方式变革的响应。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：透明同行评审制度的利弊与科学信任问题

不同观点：
• **[probably_wrong]**：认为透明同行评审可能对科学不利。主要担忧在于社交媒体上的研究者可能利用其影响力对评审结果施压，且某些群体可能利用工具对评审人员进行人身攻击。引用了ACL 2019年的调查，指出女性和有经验的研究者对公开评审的支持度较低，认为这种制度可能只对已经处于学术圈内的人有利。

• **[aDyslecticCrow]**：支持透明同行评审，认为这是提高学术信任和科学严谨性的必要步骤。尤其在AI可能进一步影响科学质量的背景下，严格的出版流程变得更加重要，透明评审能增强信任。

• **[jostmey]**：认为透明评审只解决了同行评审中的一小部分问题。真正的挑战在于评审者无法复制研究，因此只能寻找论文中的不一致之处，这可能导致对不符合预期的研究产生偏见。此外，数据造假如果合理也可能不被质疑。

• **[eig]**：赞同透明评审，认为这有助于减少大实验室通过与编辑的关系更容易在高影响力期刊上发表文章的情况。其自身从透明评审的报告中受益匪浅。

• **[trelane]**：指出透明评审揭示的争议只是更大问题的冰山一角，暗示当前评审制度存在更深层次的问题。

• **[dr_dshiv]**：认为科学界需要更多的学术社团，回顾科学历史，主张高标准的小型学术社区评审模式，而不是试图做到“客观”的现代同行评审制度。强调科学评审中“友谊”的重要性。

• **[lenerdenator]**：对透明评审的概念感到困惑，认为这应该是默认的操作方式，质疑为何现在才开始实施。

• **[WhatsTheBigIdea]**：支持透明评审是积极的一步，但认为来得太晚。强调科学本质在于质疑和怀疑，对“相信科学”的说法持批判态度，认为这是对科学基础的破坏，主张科学应被测试而非信任。

补充讨论：
- **透明评审的利弊**：支持者认为能提高信任和严谨性，反对者担忧引发社交媒体压力和人身攻击。
- **同行评审的局限性**：如无法复制研究导致的偏见和数据造假问题。
- **科学信任问题**：有观点认为科学应通过质疑和怀疑来进步，而非简单的信任。
- **历史视角**：有评论提到科学评审的历史模式，主张回归高标准的小型学术社区评审。

44292342.article_content:
Twitter

A published research paper is the result of an extensive conversation between authors and reviewers, guided by editors.
Credit: Getty
Since 2020,
Nature
has offered authors the opportunity to have their
peer-review file published alongside their paper
. Our colleagues at
Nature Communications
have been doing so since 2016
. Until now,
Nature
authors could opt in to this process of transparent peer review. From 16 June, however, new submissions of manuscripts that are published as research articles in
Nature
will automatically include a link to the reviewers’ reports and author responses.
It means that, over time, more
Nature
papers will include a peer-review file. The identity of the reviewers will remain anonymous, unless they choose otherwise — as happens now. But the exchanges between the referees and the authors will be accessible to all. Our aim in doing so is to open up what many see as the ‘black box’ of science, shedding light on how a research paper is made. This serves to increase transparency and (we hope) to build trust in the scientific process.
Research evaluation needs to change with the times
As
we have written previously
, a published research paper is the result of an extensive conversation between authors and reviewers, guided by editors. These discussions, which can last for months, aim to improve a study’s clarity and the robustness of its conclusions. It is a hugely important process that should receive increased recognition, including acknowledgement of the reviewers involved, if they choose to be named. For early-career researchers, there is great value in seeing inside a process that is key to their career development. Making peer-reviewer reports public also enriches science communication: it’s a chance to add to the ‘story’ of how a result is arrived at, or a conclusion supported, even if it includes only the perspectives of authors and reviewers. The full story of a paper is, of course, more complex, involving many other contributors.
Many people think of science as something fixed and unchanging. But scientific knowledge evolves as new or more-nuanced evidence comes to light. Scientists constantly discuss their results, yet these debates are not contained in research papers and often remain unreported in wider science-communication efforts.
Three-year trial shows support for recognizing peer reviewers
The COVID-19 pandemic provided a brief interlude during which much of the world got to see how research works,
almost in real time
. It’s easy to forget that, right from the start, we were continuously learning something new about the nature and behaviour of the SARS-CoV-2 virus. On television screens, in newspapers and on social media worldwide, scientists were discussing among themselves and with public audiences the nature of the virus, how it infects people and how it spreads. They were debating treatments and prevention methods, constantly adjusting everyone’s knowledge
as fresh evidence came to light
. And then, it went mostly back to business as usual.
We hope that publishing the peer-reviewer reports of all newly submitted
Nature
papers shows, in a small way, that this doesn’t need to remain the case.
Nature
started mandating peer review for all published research articles only in 1973 (
M. Baldwin
Notes Rec.
69
, 337–352; 2015
). But the convention in most fields is still to keep the content of these peer-review exchanges confidential. That has meant that the wider research community, and the world, has had few opportunities to learn what is discussed.
Peer review improves papers. The exchanges between authors and referees should be seen as a crucial part of the scientific record, just as they are a key part of doing and disseminating research.

data.title: Should we design for iffy internet?
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了2025年美国仍存在互联网不稳定的问题，尤其是对于网络开发者和软件设计者而言，不应假设所有用户都有高速网络。作者引用了联邦通信委员会（FCC）和国家教育统计中心（NCES）的数据，指出约97%的美国家庭能接入互联网，但网速常限于25Mbps下行和3Mbps上行，且延迟可能较高。城市区域网络较好，而农村地区较差。作者建议，在设计软件时应考虑这些网络限制，以免排除农村用户，但具体设计需根据目标市场决定。文章还提到学生网络接入数据，以进一步说明网络不均的问题。总的来说，开发者需在设计时考虑不同网络环境，以确保更广泛的用户覆盖。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何应对不稳定网络环境下的产品设计，以及是否应将技术架构设计为始终在线、始终连接。

不同观点：
• [hosh] 认为当前的商业模式鼓励持续联网和计费，这与月度经常性收入有关，甚至硬件公司也想参与（如HP打印机和授权墨盒）。但他提出另一种视角，认为应该从文明韧性的角度看待网络设计，尤其是在战争区域或网络通信被针对的情况下。他质疑是否应该假设未来网络总是处于连接状态，并担忧技术是否会集中在少数人手中。

• [steelegbr] 强调通过移动网络（3G/4G/5G）的体验说明设计时考虑不稳定网络的重要性。他指出，许多应用在遇到网络波动时会出现挂起，尤其是在流媒体或WebSocket应用中，这是一个实际存在的问题。

• [dbetteridge] 建议假设网络环境很差来进行设计，这样即使用户拥有良好网络，也会对产品的表现感到满意。此外，这还能吸引更多来自农村地区或网络不稳定的潜在客户。

• [pfych] 通过个人经验说明在糟糕的网络条件下使用产品遇到的困难，并反思在开发新功能时应更多考虑不稳定连接，比如设计易于解析的加载状态、更好的超时提醒、将计算移至客户端等。

• [londons_explore] 指出WhatsApp和OpenAI API在糟糕网络条件下表现优异，例如在网络中断几分钟后仍能获取GPT4的回答。

• [MatthiasPortzel] 提到某些地区（如北达科他州）拥有良好的千兆光纤网络，暗示网络条件因地而异。

• [metalman] 分享了自己仅依赖移动网络的经验，指出不仅网络不稳定，设备本身也可能因设置问题出现故障。他通过实验解决了信号弱的问题，但仍有一些地方信号不稳定，只能使用语音和文本。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应将技术架构设计为始终在线、始终连接。一部分人如[hosh]对此持怀疑态度，认为应更多考虑文明韧性，而不是只为商业利益设计。而其他人如[steelegbr]、[dbetteridge]和[pfych]则关注实际应用中的用户体验，强调设计应适应不稳定的网络环境。

• 一些成功的案例如WhatsApp和OpenAI API被提出，表明在技术上实现良好的不稳定网络适应性是可行的。

• 网络条件的地域差异也被提及，显示出设计适应性强的产品在不同地区具有重要意义。

44290580.article_content:
Should we design for iffy internet?
Brian Hicks, June 16, 2025
I keep hearing claims like this:
Not everyone in the US has access to stable, reliable internet, even in 2025.
Web developers should stop assuming people have fast internet connections and slim their payloads accordingly.
This seems intuitively true to meâprogrammers are gonna have better connectivity because that takes money, and programmers are well-paid. But what's the actual scope of the problem?
I dug around, and here's some data. My goal here is not to beat anyone over the head with "THOU SHALT NOT ASSUME GOOD INTERNET" but to give an idea about the scope of broadband rollout in the US in a way that can help inform choices we make when designing software.
If you don't feel like reading this whole thing, here's the bottom line up front:
you can probably assume internet access in somewhere around 97% of US households, but you should not assume that it's better than around 25Mbps down and 3Mbps up, and latency may be significantly worse than you previously assumed. This is likely worse for B2C software than B2B.
I'm going to pull from two US government agencies here: the
Federal Communications Commission (FCC)
and the
National Center for Education Statistics (NCES)
(part of the Department of Education.) All the data I'm referencing was published well before the current administration started gutting the bureaucracy, so I think it's fairly reliable.
Assumptions
Before we begin, there are a bunch of ways to define "stable" or "reliable" internet connections. For the purposes of this post, I'm defining that as a
terrestrial link with at least 25Mbps down and 3Mbps up.
Terrestrial becauseâwell, have you ever tried to use a satellite connection for anything real? Latency is awful, and the systems tend to go down in bad weather. They also have had fairly low data caps historically so you had to use your connection judiciously, although this may be changing.
1
2
25/3Mpbs because that's a fairly common cable package speed, and also around the minimum Iâve been able to use modern SaaS apps on without it getting ridiculously frustrating.
Zoom says
you need 1â4 Mbps in both directions to do a video call.
The FCC's broadband map lets you set both these criteria. Let's have a look at it.
The FCC Broadband Map
The FCC tracks access to broadband internet in the US. As a result, they publish a map that's more accurate than the maps you see from ISPs. This isn't
completely
error-free, but individuals and companies can both submit data on coverage at a street address level and challenge inaccuracies in the existing data. For our purposes, I think it's good enough!
I'm going to grab some screenshots of the map to fix it at the current data for discussion. That way we can get an idea about regional coverage.
Strangely, they don't let you zoom out enough to grab a screenshot of the whole country so I'm going to look at the west. That'll get both urban and rural coverage, as well as several famously internet-y locations (San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle.)
If you want to follow along or compare how the data has changed since this post was published, you can get the map yourself at
broadbandmap.fcc.gov
.
First, here's a hex map of coverage using the criteria we set above. The darker each hex is, the higher the percent coverage within it. Dark blue is 100%, white is 0%, grays or faded blues are in between.
This shows pretty much what I'd expect: coverage is fine in and around cities and less great in rural areas.
3
(The Dakotas are an interesting exception;
there's a co-op up there
that connected a ton of folks with gigabit fiber. Pretty cool!)
Although, remember that these are
minimum
criteria. When I'm building software, I'm mostly doing it on my home internet. A test just now says I get 367/71Mpbs. What does the country look like if I were to expect all my users to have similar connections? The map lets us filter for 250/25; let's look:
Cities are pretty much unchanged, but rural coverage gets much worse. (Except again for North Dakota, the reigning champion of rural fiber.)
So what does this tell us about how we should design software? One big takeaway: if you design for the
availability
of fast internet connections, you'll exclude many people in rural areas.
This may or may not be OK for your marketâ"good internet" tends to be in population centers, and population centers tend to contain more businesses and consumers. You have to make that call!
However, it's also worth keeping in mind that this is a map of commercial availability, not market penetration. Hypothetically, you could get the average speed of a US residential internet connection, but the FCC doesn't make such a statistic available.
4
However, we have another source of data!
Student Internet Access
The US Department of Education occasionally tracks student internet access. Since classwork and homework have moved more online (especially during the early days of COVID) it's useful data for pol

44290580.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何应对不稳定网络环境下的产品设计，以及是否应将技术架构设计为始终在线、始终连接。

不同观点：
• [hosh] 认为当前的商业模式鼓励持续联网和计费，这与月度经常性收入有关，甚至硬件公司也想参与（如HP打印机和授权墨盒）。但他提出另一种视角，认为应该从文明韧性的角度看待网络设计，尤其是在战争区域或网络通信被针对的情况下。他质疑是否应该假设未来网络总是处于连接状态，并担忧技术是否会集中在少数人手中。

• [steelegbr] 强调通过移动网络（3G/4G/5G）的体验说明设计时考虑不稳定网络的重要性。他指出，许多应用在遇到网络波动时会出现挂起，尤其是在流媒体或WebSocket应用中，这是一个实际存在的问题。

• [dbetteridge] 建议假设网络环境很差来进行设计，这样即使用户拥有良好网络，也会对产品的表现感到满意。此外，这还能吸引更多来自农村地区或网络不稳定的潜在客户。

• [pfych] 通过个人经验说明在糟糕的网络条件下使用产品遇到的困难，并反思在开发新功能时应更多考虑不稳定连接，比如设计易于解析的加载状态、更好的超时提醒、将计算移至客户端等。

• [londons_explore] 指出WhatsApp和OpenAI API在糟糕网络条件下表现优异，例如在网络中断几分钟后仍能获取GPT4的回答。

• [MatthiasPortzel] 提到某些地区（如北达科他州）拥有良好的千兆光纤网络，暗示网络条件因地而异。

• [metalman] 分享了自己仅依赖移动网络的经验，指出不仅网络不稳定，设备本身也可能因设置问题出现故障。他通过实验解决了信号弱的问题，但仍有一些地方信号不稳定，只能使用语音和文本。

• 争议的焦点在于是否应将技术架构设计为始终在线、始终连接。一部分人如[hosh]对此持怀疑态度，认为应更多考虑文明韧性，而不是只为商业利益设计。而其他人如[steelegbr]、[dbetteridge]和[pfych]则关注实际应用中的用户体验，强调设计应适应不稳定的网络环境。

data.title: The Humble Programmer (1972)
data.author: squircle
data.article_summary:
Edsger W. Dijkstra's "The Humble Programmer" reflects on the slow emergence of programming as a recognized profession in the early 1950s in the Netherlands. Initially, programming was not seen as an intellectually respectable discipline, lacking a solid theoretical foundation. Dijkstra recounts a pivotal conversation with his boss, A. van Wijngaarden, who encouraged him to help establish programming as a respected field. This conversation shifted Dijkstra's career path from theoretical physics to programming. He also humorously notes that when he married in 1957, the authorities did not recognize "programmer" as a valid profession.

Dijkstra describes the early days of computing when computers were unique, experimental machines, and the focus was on hardware. Programmers were largely overlooked, as attention centered on keeping the machines running. The essay highlights how past perceptions still influence misunderstandings about programming today. Dijkstra emphasizes the evolution of computing and the growing recognition of programming as a critical intellectual endeavor.

不同观点：
• [varjag] 认为编程在过去几十年里可能被高薪对待，且当前社会对程序员的表现和产品日益不满，这可能预示薪资下降。这与程序员过去的工作质量不佳有关。

• [stereolambda] 比较了过去与现代对编程和社会期望的视角转变，指出编程语言作为思维工具的角色变化，并提到Golang和JavaScript/TypeScript的演变。
• [selcuka] 引用了对FORTRAN的批评，认为其不再适合现代编程思维，但注意到其标准仍在更新。
• [b0a04gl] 认为Dijkstra的观点经受了时间的考验，指出团队在追求快速输出而非清洁设计时常常遇到问题。
• [enord] 认为Dijkstra的尖锐批评虽然正确，但其精英主义倾向可能让许多人不快，指出追求程序可管理性可能牺牲执行速度和产品开发效率。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是程序员薪资是否过高及其未来趋势，以及程序员过去工作质量对当前行业状况的影响。
• 另一个焦点是编程语言和系统设计中的优化问题，特别是在现代硬件环境下的内存管理和计算效率。
• 对Dijkstra观点的评价也存在分歧，一些人赞赏其深刻见解，另一些人则批评其精英主义和可能带来的实际操作困难。
• 编程语言的历史和演变，特别是如FORTRAN和Coq等语言的角色和适用性，也被广泛讨论。

ACM Turing Lecture 1972
EWD340
The Humble Programmer
by
Edsger W. Dijkstra
As a result of a long sequence of coincidences I entered the programming profession officially on the first spring morning of 1952 and as far as I have been able to trace, I was the first Dutchman to do so in my country. In retrospect the most amazing thing was the slowness with which, at least in my part of the world, the programming profession emerged, a slowness which is now hard to believe. But I am grateful for two vivid recollections from that period that establish that slowness beyond any doubt.
After having programmed for some three years, I had a discussion with A. van Wijngaarden, who was then my boss at the Mathematical Centre in Amsterdam, a discussion for which I shall remain grateful to him as long as I live. The point was that I was supposed to study theoretical physics at the University of Leiden simultaneously, and as I found the two activities harder and harder to combine, I had to make up my mind, either to stop programming and become a real, respectable theoretical physicist, or to carry my study of physics to a formal completion only, with a minimum of effort, and to become....., yes what? A programmer? But was that a respectable profession? For after all, what was programming? Where was the sound body of knowledge that could support it as an intellectually respectable discipline? I remember quite vividly how I envied my hardware colleagues, who, when asked about their professional competence, could at least point out that they knew everything about vacuum tubes, amplifiers and the rest, whereas I felt that, when faced with that question, I would stand empty-handed. Full of misgivings I knocked on van Wijngaarden’s office door, asking him whether I could “speak to him for a moment”; when I left his office a number of hours later, I was another person. For after having listened to my problems patiently, he agreed that up till that moment there was not much of a programming discipline, but then he went on to explain quietly that automatic computers were here to stay, that we were just at the beginning and could not I be one of the persons called to make programming a respectable discipline in the years to come? This was a turning point in my life and I completed my study of physics formally as quickly as I could. One moral of the above story is, of course, that we must be very careful when we give advice to younger people; sometimes they follow it!
Another two years later, in 1957, I married and Dutch marriage rites require you to state your profession and I stated that I was a programmer. But the municipal authorities of the town of Amsterdam did not accept it on the grounds that there was no such profession. And, believe it or not, but under the heading “profession” my marriage act shows the ridiculous entry “theoretical physicist”!
So much for the slowness with which I saw the programming profession emerge in my own country. Since then I have seen more of the world, and it is my general impression that in other countries, apart from a possible shift of dates, the growth pattern has been very much the same.
Let me try to capture the situation in those old days in a little bit more detail, in the hope of getting a better understanding of the situation today. While we pursue our analysis, we shall see how many common misunderstandings about the true nature of the programming task can be traced back to that now distant past.
The first automatic electronic computers were all unique, single-copy machines and they were all to be found in an environment with the exciting flavour of an experimental laboratory. Once the vision of the automatic computer was there, its realisation was a tremendous challenge to the electronic technology then available, and one thing is certain: we cannot deny the courage of the groups that decided to try and build such a fantastic piece of equipment. For fantastic pieces of equipment they were: in retrospect one can only wonder that those first machines worked at all, at least sometimes. The overwhelming problem was to get and keep the machine in working order. The preoccupation with the physical aspects of automatic computing is still reflected in the names of the older scientific societies in the field, such as the Association for Computing Machinery or the British Computer Society, names in which explicit reference is made to the physical equipment.
What about the poor programmer? Well, to tell the honest truth: he was hardly noticed. For one thing, the first machines were so bulky that you could hardly move them and besides that, they required such extensive maintenance that it was quite natural that the place where people tried to use the machine was the same laboratory where the machine had been developed. data.title: The drawbridges come up: the dream of a interconnected context ecosystem is over
data.author: dbreunig
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了AI时代下MCP（多应用连接点）技术的发展，与Web 2.0时代有相似之处。在Web 2.0时期，各类应用通过API实现互通，但随着平台竞争加剧，主要赢家开始限制数据访问，API变得复杂且受控。如今，MCPs也面临类似情况。例如，Slack限制第三方访问其消息，X平台修改协议禁止内容用于训练AI，Anthropic和Google等公司因竞争关系调整合作。文章指出，MCPs虽有潜力连接各类应用和数据，但最终可能仅作为受控工具存在，而非自由交换的桥梁。平台间的竞争和数据壁垒将限制MCPs的广泛应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：平台API的管理、开放与竞争问题

不同观点：
• **Permit**：认为平台在取得市场主导地位后，会通过复杂的API控制和定价层级限制竞争，特别是以隐私问题为由。例如Twitter限制第三方客户端用户数量。同时指出开放API可能带来数据滥用问题，如Facebook的数据丑闻。

• **walterbell**：强调监管对互操作性和竞争的必要性，列举了多个国际上针对大型科技公司的反垄断案例，如欧盟的移动和消息互操作性要求，以及美国对Google和Facebook/Meta的法律行动。

• **teleforce**：提出Braid项目的倡议，旨在为网络创建一个完全互连的生态系统，并提供了相关资源链接，建议停止使用REST进行状态同步。

• **armchairhacker**：反对通过监管强制开放API，认为应去除阻止数据抓取的法规，并提出公司需要新的 monetization 路径以应对收入损失和非法抓取问题。

• **exabrial**：批评OAuth/API被用于垃圾营销，原本美好的技术被滥用。

• **bsenftner**：对MCP（多方计算协议）持怀疑态度，认为其理想化且不切实际。

• **seydor**：乐观地认为LLM（大型语言模型）能够理解自然语言，用户应能通过AI访问自己的数据，而不应被大公司限制。

• **eadmund**：指出服务器和软件工程师的成本问题，认为广告是支付成本的一种方式，但不利于集成。建议通过订阅等方式支付服务费用，并讨论了API使用的合理计划。

• **renewiltord**：认为平台不可能免费提供他人 monetize 的机会，列举了imgur和Reddit的例子，指出API开放可能导致用户数据泄露和公司收入损失问题，并探讨了可能的API收费模式。

• **tempodox**：认为平台的限制和控制是资本主义的自然结果，任何技术都无法根本改变这一现象，平台的蜜月期只是为了吸引用户。

• **yapyap** 和 **bigmattystyles** 的评论较为简短，前者调侃AI的内部竞争，后者可能是对SAP相关问题表达无奈。

44294526.article_content:
Jun 16, 2025
MCP
LLM
AI
WEB 2.0
MOATS
The Drawbridges Go Up
The AI Era is Speedrunning the Web 2.0 Story: Integrations Will Be Tightly Governed
The chatter around
MCPs
has been reminding me of
Web 2.0
. MCPs have become a rallying point for a larger vision of the future, where LLMs are connected to all the data and apps they’ll ever need, allowing them to easily perform all the rote tasks we’d like to avoid.
Web 2.0 described a similar vision (among other visions), where interconnected services would allow apps to leverage all your data, no matter where it resides.
For a while, every app published an API. Consultants made bank helping governments and corporations set up their own APIs. Many API standards emerged and withered, and we waded through the various security issues until we stabilized on a set of norms. Things were pretty good!
But it didn’t last.
Once network effects crowded a few winners, the drawbridges slowly pulled up.
Previously simple APIs evolved into complicated layers of access controls and pricing tiers
. Winning platforms adjusted their APIs so you could
support
their platforms, but not build anything competitive. Perhaps the best example of this was Twitter’s 2012 policy adjustment which
limited client 3rd party apps to a maximum of 100,000 users
(
they’ve since cut off all 3rd party clients
).
The Web 2.0 dream of unfettered free exchange evolved into tightly governed one-way interfaces. Today there are plenty of APIs to support ad buying and posting on Facebook, Google, or Twitter, but barely any that allow you to consume data.
We’re already seeing a similar narrative play out with MCPs.
MCPs are a touchstone technology, a feature that embodies the dream for
what could be
. We want LLMs to be able to access our apps and data so they can effectively answer questions or perform tasks for us. The problem is each platform likely has its own AI, which they’d prefer we’d use.
Let’s look at what happened in the last two weeks:
“
Slack, a Salesforce-owned workplace messaging app, recently blocked other software firms from searching or storing Slack messages
.”
“
X has changed its developer agreement to prevent third parties from using the platform’s content to train large language models
.”
Anthropic, “
cut Windsurf’s direct access to Anthropic’s Claude AI models largely because of rumors and reports that OpenAI, its largest competitor, is acquiring the AI coding assistant
.”
“
Google, the largest customer of Scale AI, plans to cut ties with Scale after news broke that rival Meta, opens new tab is taking a 49% stake in the AI data-labeling startup
.”
The drawbridges are coming up quickly, accelerated by consolidation. Data remains a moat and our dreams of proliferating MCPs are likely a mirage (at least for non-paying users). MCPs, like the APIs of Web 2.0, will shake out as merely a protocol, not a movement. It will be a mechanism for easy LLM tool use, but those tools will be tightly governed and controlled.
Sure, build an MCP for your app or service. But don’t expect the platforms to let you compete easily.

data.title: Text-to-LoRA: Hypernetwork that generates task-specific LLM adapters (LoRAs)
data.author: dvrp
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为Text-to-LoRA（T2L）的项目，该项目通过文本任务描述生成适用于特定基准任务的LoRA（低秩适配器），从而快速调整大型语言模型（LLM）。项目提供了安装指南、演示示例及评估方法。用户可以通过命令行生成和评估LoRA，项目支持使用不同模型如Mistral-7B和Gemma-2B。即使使用随机描述，SFT训练的T2L仍能生成合理的LoRA，但对齐描述的效果更佳。项目还提供了训练脚本，用于异步验证和LoRA基线训练，整个训练过程可能需要数天时间。

文章主要讨论了城市铁路网络的发展及其面临的挑战。19世纪，欧洲和北美的铁路进入城市时往往在城市边缘终止，原因包括市中心土地成本高、隧道技术不足以及监管限制。这导致铁路终点站集中在城市边缘，如伦敦和巴黎的铁路网络呈现“无中心轮辐”模式，而在德国，多条线路共同进入城市形成大型终点站（Hauptbahnhof）。

19世纪末，电气化和隧道技术进步催生了现代地铁，能够更灵活地在城市中运行，并与其他线路互联，避免了终点站的瓶颈问题。然而，传统铁路终点站由于容量限制和周围土地昂贵，扩展困难，成为列车班次频率的制约因素。

尽管地铁系统发展迅速，许多城市的传统铁路网络依然存在，并因建设成本高昂而比现代地铁更为广泛。文章以伦敦为例，说明这些 legacy 网络至今仍在使用。

This is the lead story of the new issue of Works in Progress,
Issue 19
. Read the full issue, including stories on
how to redraw cities
and
the secret history of inflation targeting
, on
our website.
In the nineteenth century, the societies of Europe and North America were profoundly transformed by the vast railway networks they built. When these railway networks entered cities, however, they faced a crucial problem: they had to stop. Rather than carrying on through the city, it was common for them to terminate on its edge.
In part, this was due to the high cost of acquiring land in urban areas. It was also a technological problem: the
tunneling technologies
that would enable railways to run into the centre underground without destroying everything in their path had not yet been invented. Finally, the problem was sometimes regulatory as well: in cities such as London railways
were prohibited
from penetrating too deep into the urban area.
The result was that nineteenth century railways often terminated roughly wherever the city limits were when they were built. Some Victorian urban networks, like those of London and Paris, thus resemble a vast hubless wheel whose spokes do not quite join one another in the middle. In other cases, the lines circled round the city and then all entered it at the same point, terminating together in one huge station. This model was common in Germany, so that stations of this sort are still sometimes known by the German name
Hauptbahnhof
(literally: main station).
London in the mid-nineteenth century: the hubless wheel model. Source:
Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division.
At the end of the nineteenth century, electrification and improvements in tunneling technology led to the emergence of a new kind of railway: the modern metro. Metros were a huge advance in three ways. First, they could go anywhere in the city. Second, metro lines could easily interconnect with one other, meaning that passengers could use the network to travel swiftly from any part of the city to any other part of the city, rather than merely going from a suburb to the edge of the center. Third, the lines were not bottlenecked by the capacity of a central terminus.
Inner-city termini like London Waterloo and the Gare du Nord in Paris have always handled a complex range of intercity and suburban trains, so delays on any one service can easily propagate over to others. To stop every small delay from generating a huge chain of further delays, tracks and platforms have to be used far below their theoretical maximum capacity: the system can only operate smoothly by preserving a great deal of redundancy. Trains therefore wait around at the terminus for longer than strictly necessary, to recover from delays.
This, in turn, means that termini have to be massive, and in the age of steam, this was compounded by needing to have room to turn around and store steam locomotives and carriages. Today, the Gare du Nord has 28 tracks above ground, and Waterloo has 24.
The giant Gare du Nord (right) and the Gare de l’Est in Paris. Source:
Wikimedia Commons
.
As demand for railway services grew, these termini filled up. But expanding central termini is rarely straightforward: they are typically surrounded by expensive land containing dense urban fabric which would have to be demolished. Furthermore, they are often located on viaducts or in a trench, which makes their expansion technically difficult. Over time, terminus capacity thus generally became the binding constraint on the number of trains that could be run in and out of the urban core, limiting the frequency of both the suburban trains and intercity services.
Metros, by contrast, could get away with much smaller termini. A typical metro runs a very simple service pattern: every train stops at every station, with few branch lines, and shares no track with any other services, so delays are much less likely. A metro train can easily turn around in well under five minutes, so its terminus only requires two or three platforms.
In the first decades of the twentieth century, metro lines were built in cities across Europe and North America like Paris, Tokyo, London, Barcelona, and New York. In all of these cities, however, metro lines were built to supplement the Victorian legacy networks, rather than to replace them. As a result, the legacy networks are still there today.

data.title: AMD's Pre-Zen Interconnect: Testing Trinity's Northbridge
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了AMD在Zen架构之前使用的互连技术，特别是Trinity APU的北桥设计。Trinity APU结合了Piledriver CPU模块和Terascale 3 iGPU，其片上网络类似于早期的Athlon 64北桥设计。北桥运行在独立的电压和频率域上，采用两级交叉开关（XBAR）设置，用于处理内存和IO请求。CPU核心通过系统请求接口（SRI）连接到XBAR，XBAR负责将请求路由到内存控制器（MCT）或IO设备。

Trinity的iGPU有自己的图形内存控制器（GMC），通过“Garlic”链接直接连接到DRAM，绕过MCT以避免缓存一致性问题和带宽争用。同时，GPU通过“Onion”链接连接到XBAR，类似于其他IO设备。MCT和GMC通过限制 outstanding requests 和使用优先级机制来确保CPU和GPU不会互相争用内存带宽。这种设计使得Trinity的iGPU能有效利用内存带宽，区别于纯CPU产品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于AMD芯片架构的技术讨论及其历史演变，包括对内存控制、缓存一致性及驱动支持的分析。

不同观点：
• bee_rider认为文章保持技术和客观性是好的，但提出是否更值得探讨AMD在Zen架构之前的失败经历，或者分析这些早期设计如何为Zen架构的成功打下基础。这暗示了对历史回顾和失败分析的兴趣。
• freeqaz关注文章中的术语使用问题，指出“DCT”在文中未定义，并提出可能的解释（如DRAM内存控制器或Discrete Cosine Transform）。freeqaz建议将DCT替换为更明确的MCT（内存控制器），以避免混淆。
• jauntywundrkind详细分析了AMD在早期架构中为避免缓存一致性问题而采取的复杂设计（如Garlic和Onion总线）。他同时对比了现代的Infinity Fabric设计，认为现代设计在概念上更简单，但缓存一致性的处理依然复杂。
• 对于GPU的多芯片缓存和内存控制设计（如6800xt中的Memory Control Die），jauntywundrkind表示好奇，认为AMD需要深入理解各芯片间的内存分配和缓存一致性问题。

• jauntywundrkind进一步提到Linux系统下旧款GPU（如Trinity）的游戏兼容性问题，指出开源驱动（如radeonsi）仍在不断改进。他特别提到驱动在多线程支持上的重大进展，并引用了Phoronix网站的相关报道。

Today, AMD’s Infinity Fabric interconnect is ubiquitous across the company’s lineup. Infinity Fabric provides well-defined interfaces to a transport layer, and lets different functional blocks treat the interconnect as a black box. The system worked well enough to let AMD create integrated GPU products all the way from the Steam Deck’s tiny van Gogh APU, to giant systems packing four MI300A chips. Across all those offerings, Infinity Fabric enables coherent memory access as CPU and GPU requests converge to Coherent Slaves (CS-es), which have a probe filter and can request data from the appropriate source.
AMD was also trying to build powerful iGPUs over a decade ago, but their interconnect looked very different at the time. Their Northbridge architecture owes its name to the Athlon 64 era, when AMD brought the chipset northbridge’s functionality onto the CPU die. AMD’s engineers likely didn’t envision needing to tightly integrate a GPU during Athlon 64’s development, so the interconnect was designed to tie together a few CPU cores and service memory requests with low latency. But then AMD acquired ATI, and set about trying to take advantage of their new graphics talent by building powerful iGPUs.
“Trinity” is an AMD Accelerated Processing Unit (APU) from 2012. It combines two dual-threaded Piledriver CPU modules with a 6-SIMD Terascale 3 iGPU. Here I’ll be looking into AMD’s second generation iGPU interconnect with the A8-5600K, a slightly cut-down Trinity implementation with four Terascale 3 SIMDs enabled and CPU boost clocks dropped from 4.2 to 3.9 GHz. I’m testing the chip on a MSI FM2-A75MA-E35 board with 16 GB of Kingston DDR3-1866 10-10-9-26 memory.
Trinity’s on-die network resembles that of AMD’s first APU, Llano, and has clear similarities to AMD’s Athlon 64 Northbridge. The Northbridge sits on a separate voltage and frequency domain, and runs at 1.8 GHz on the A8-5600K. It uses a two-level crossbar setup. CPU cores connect to a System Request Interface (SRI), which routes requests onto a set of queues. Most memory requests head to a System Request Queue (SRQ). The SRI also accepts incoming probes on a separate queue, and routes them to the CPU cores. A second level crossbar, simply called the XBAR, connects with the SRI’s various queues and routes requests to IO and memory. The XBAR can handle IO-to-IO communication too, though such traffic is rare on consumer systems.
On Trinity, the XBAR’s scheduler (XCS) has 40 entries, making it slightly smaller than the 64 entry XCS on desktop and server Piledriver chips. AMD defaults to a 22+10+8 entry split between the SRI, Memory Controller (MCT),and upstream channel, though the BIOS can opt for a different XCS entry allocation. The XBAR sends memory requests to the MCT, which prioritizes requests based on type and age, and includes a strided-access prefetcher. Like Infinity Fabric’s CS, the MCT is responsible for ensuring cache coherency and can send probes back to the XBAR. The MCT also translates physical addresses to “normalized” addresses that only cover the memory space backed by DRAM.
All AMD CPUs from Trinity’s era use a similar SRI+XBAR setup, but Trinity’s iGPU sets it apart from CPU-only products. The iGPU gets its own Graphics Memory Controller (GMC), which arbitrates between different request types and schedules requests to maximize DRAM bandwidth utilization. Thus the GMC performs an analogous role to the MCT on the CPU side. A “Radeon Memory Bus” connects the GMC to the DRAM controllers, bypassing the MCT. AMD documentation occasionally refers to the Radeon Memory Bus as “Garlic”, likely a holdover from internal names used during Llano’s development.
A second control link hooks the GPU into the XBAR, much like any other IO device. Previously, the control link was called the “Fusion Control Link”, or “Onion”. I’ll use “Garlic” and “Onion” to refer to the two links because those names are shorter.
The “Garlic” Link (Radeon Memory Bus)
Trinity’s “Garlic” link lets the GPU saturate DRAM bandwidth. It bypasses the MCT and therefore bypasses the Northbridge’s cache coherency mechanisms. That’s a key design feature, because CPUs and GPUs usually don’t share data. Snooping the CPU caches for GPU memory requests would waste power and flood the interconnect with probes, most of which would miss.
Bypassing the MCT also skips the Northbridge’s regular memory prioritization mechanism, so the MCT and GMC have various mechanisms to keep the CPU and GPU from starving each other of memory bandwidth. First, the MCT and GMC can limit how many outstanding requests they have on the DRAM controller queues (DCQs). Then, the

data.article_summary: 《Fun with Telnet》一文介绍了通过Telnet体验各种有趣的文字动画和游戏。作者提到一个受《星球大战》启发的ASCII动画，用户可以通过`telnet towel.blinkenlights.nl 23`观看。此外，文章还列举了其他可以通过Telnet访问的资源，如国际象棋、太空战斗游戏、双陆棋以及可缩放的世界地图。作者提醒，由于Telnet通信是明文传输，使用时需注意保密。文章鼓励读者探索Telnet的趣味旧世界，并提供了相关链接和支持方式。

data.title: Pitfalls of premature closure with LLM assisted coding
data.author: shayonj
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了医疗和软件开发中常见的认知错误——“过早关闭”（premature closure）。在医疗案例中，多名医生因初始诊断看似合理而忽略了更严重的问题，险些漏诊致命的主动脉夹层。同样，在软件开发中，AI助手提供的建议往往表面完美，容易让人不再深入探索其他可能的解决方案，从而错过更根本的改进机会。文章强调，在简单任务中，AI能提高效率，但在复杂问题中，过度依赖首个建议可能导致误判和次优解。开发者应警惕这种“完美方案的诱惑”，保持批判性思维。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在代码生成和问题解决中的有效使用及其局限性

不同观点：
• stillpointlab：认为AI的表现取决于输入的质量。如果问题定义明确、上下文详实、代码审查仔细，AI可以生成高质量的代码。他将AI视作初级工程师，既给予一定的自主性，也会严格验证输出结果。他强调多问替代方案，并保持怀疑态度。
• jbellis：赞同stillpointlab的观点，并指出审查人类编写的代码时也存在类似问题。他认为在审查代码前，自己需要有一个初步的正确解决方案，才能有效进行审查。
• danielbln：指出原文未提及使用的模型和环境细节，导致建议的具体操作性不强。他通过实验发现Claude 4能识别代码中的问题，但对文章缺乏具体细节表示担忧。
• lubujackson：认为当前的LLM可以处理不同层次的抽象和焦点，但需要识别和隔离“层次”来解决问题。他建议通过多层次的提问来逐步改进代码，并认为如果模型能从架构角度出发，可能会更有效。
• mrklol：强调需要提供详尽的上下文信息给模型，以帮助其发现代码中的问题。他认为模型的有效性依赖于用户提供的输入质量。
• nonethewiser：认为讨论的重点在于验证LLM的输出，并提出“ premature closure”风险，即过早接受LLM的结果而不进行充分验证。他称之为使用LLM的“原罪”。
• MontagFTB：认为这种问题在AI出现之前就已经存在，指出人类在软件开发中早就面临类似的问题，如代码臃肿和不稳定的代码库。

补充讨论：
• suddenlybananas：对文章的布局持批评态度，认为其结构奇怪且像一首糟糕的诗。

争议焦点：
• LLM生成代码的有效性及其依赖的输入质量。
• 验证LLM输出结果的重要性及“premature closure”风险。
• 文章具体操作性的缺乏及其对建议实用性的影响。

44277284.article_content:
A 51-year-old man walked into the emergency room with chest pain. The symptoms seemed clear enough: elevated blood pressure, chest discomfort, some cardiac irregularities. The emergency physician, attending doctor, and cardiologist all converged on the same diagnosis—acute coronary syndrome or accelerated hypertension. The classic signs of anything more serious simply weren’t there.
But one hospitalist wasn’t satisfied. Despite multiple colleagues ruling out aortic dissection as unlikely, something felt incomplete. The pieces fit the common diagnosis, but not perfectly. A CT scan revealed what everyone had nearly missed: a life-threatening Stanford Type A aortic dissection that could have been fatal if left untreated.
This
medical case study
illustrates
“premature closure”
—a cognitive error where physicians latch onto an initial diagnosis and fail to consider reasonable alternatives. In this case, the atypical presentation led multiple experienced doctors to anchor on the most probable explanation while nearly missing a critical, less common condition.
The same pattern is emerging in software development as AI coding assistants become more sophisticated. The models are so good now that their first suggestion often looks not just plausible, but convincing. Professional formatting, clean code, proper naming conventions—everything appears right. And therein lies the trap.
The allure of the perfect-looking solution
Consider this scenario: You’re debugging a performance issue, and your AI assistant immediately suggests adding an index on a specific column. The suggestion comes with clean SQL, a proper migration script, and even considerations for naming conventions. It looks professional, addresses the immediate symptoms, and would probably work.
CREATE
INDEX
CONCURRENTLY idx_orders_customer_id
ON
orders (customer_id);
But what if the real issue is an N+1 query pattern that the index would merely mask? What if the performance problem stems from inefficient data modeling that a different approach might solve more elegantly? By accepting that first suggestion, you might miss opportunities for more fundamental improvements.
The AI’s suggestion isn’t wrong—it might be perfectly adequate. The issue is that we’re increasingly likely to stop exploring once we have something that looks right.
When speed becomes the enemy
There’s an undeniable ROI argument for AI-assisted development. If an AI can suggest the correct fix for a flaky spec, identify the PR that caused an exception spike, or pinpoint a workflow causing availability issues—all for minimal cost and time investment—the engineering time saved is enormous.
But here’s where it gets tricky: by incentivizing speed and ROI, we risk creating a perception where the first plausible solution becomes the default choice. This manifests as technical docs and PRs (code changes) that feel “one-shotted,” where deeper probing reveals that the author hasn’t fully explored the problem space.
The paradox is that the better AI gets, the more this becomes a problem (debatable?). When suggestions are obviously flawed, we naturally dig deeper. When they’re 85% correct and professionally formatted, our critical thinking muscles don’t get the same workout.
The spectrum of AI-appropriate tasks
Not all development tasks carry the same risk of premature closure. There’s a meaningful distinction between predictable, consistent work and complex problems with multiple valid approaches.
Menial tasks where AI excels
For routine tasks, AI shines. These are scenarios with well-established patterns and minimal variation:

44277284.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了医疗和软件开发中常见的认知错误——“过早关闭”（premature closure）。在医疗案例中，多名医生因初始诊断看似合理而忽略了更严重的问题，险些漏诊致命的主动脉夹层。同样，在软件开发中，AI助手提供的建议往往表面完美，容易让人不再深入探索其他可能的解决方案，从而错过更根本的改进机会。文章强调，在简单任务中，AI能提高效率，但在复杂问题中，过度依赖首个建议可能导致误判和次优解。开发者应警惕这种“完美方案的诱惑”，保持批判性思维。
44277284.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在代码生成和问题解决中的有效使用及其局限性

不同观点：
• stillpointlab：认为AI的表现取决于输入的质量。如果问题定义明确、上下文详实、代码审查仔细，AI可以生成高质量的代码。他将AI视作初级工程师，既给予一定的自主性，也会严格验证输出结果。他强调多问替代方案，并保持怀疑态度。
• jbellis：赞同stillpointlab的观点，并指出审查人类编写的代码时也存在类似问题。他认为在审查代码前，自己需要有一个初步的正确解决方案，才能有效进行审查。
• danielbln：指出原文未提及使用的模型和环境细节，导致建议的具体操作性不强。他通过实验发现Claude 4能识别代码中的问题，但对文章缺乏具体细节表示担忧。
• lubujackson：认为当前的LLM可以处理不同层次的抽象和焦点，但需要识别和隔离“层次”来解决问题。他建议通过多层次的提问来逐步改进代码，并认为如果模型能从架构角度出发，可能会更有效。
• mrklol：强调需要提供详尽的上下文信息给模型，以帮助其发现代码中的问题。他认为模型的有效性依赖于用户提供的输入质量。
• nonethewiser：认为讨论的重点在于验证LLM的输出，并提出“ premature closure”风险，即过早接受LLM的结果而不进行充分验证。他称之为使用LLM的“原罪”。
• MontagFTB：认为这种问题在AI出现之前就已经存在，指出人类在软件开发中早就面临类似的问题，如代码臃肿和不稳定的代码库。

补充讨论：
• suddenlybananas：对文章的布局持批评态度，认为其结构奇怪且像一首糟糕的诗。

争议焦点：
• LLM生成代码的有效性及其依赖的输入质量。
• 验证LLM输出结果的重要性及“premature closure”风险。
• 文章具体操作性的缺乏及其对建议实用性的影响。

data.title: How you breathe is like a fingerprint that can identify you
data.author: XzetaU8
data.article_summary: 一项研究发现，人的呼吸模式可能是独一无二的，像指纹一样可以用于身份识别，甚至能反映个体的身体和心理特征。研究团队让97名健康人佩戴特制设备，记录24小时内的呼吸模式，并通过24个参数分析数据，利用机器学习算法以高达96.8%的准确率识别个体。研究还发现，呼吸模式与体重指数（BMI）以及抑郁和焦虑水平相关，比如高BMI者的睡眠呼吸模式与低BMI者不同。这项研究发表在《Current Biology》上，表明呼吸模式可能成为一种强大的诊断工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过呼吸模式识别个人及其隐私、健康监测和实际应用的可能性

不同观点：
• **技术极客的隐私担忧**：[meindnoch] 提出，真正的隐私爱好者会使用复杂的设备（如CSPRNG）来随机化他们的呼吸模式，以避免在公共场合被识别。这表明了一种对隐私的高度关注，甚至愿意采取极端技术手段。

• **呼吸模式识别的科学依据**：[tbrownaw] 引用了实验数据，表明通过呼吸模式识别个人的准确率可以达到96.8%。讨论中强调了数据参数的选择对准确率的影响，并指出身体活动可能会导致结果的差异。

• **呼吸的个体差异**：[BLKNSLVR] 和 [bradley13] 都提到呼吸声音的个体差异，包括在厕所隔间中尝试通过呼吸声识别他人，以及鼻腔不对称对呼吸模式的影响。这表明呼吸声音和模式可能具有独特性。

• **呼吸监测的技术实现**：[qwertox] 分享了自己利用传感器和磁铁进行呼吸监测的实验项目，虽然未完成，但表明了技术实现的可能性。

• **呼吸与健康的关系**：[eimrine] 提到呼吸与个人舒适度和氧气需求的关系，[Noelia-] 则关注呼吸模式识别在健康和心理状态监测中的潜力，同时也表达了对隐私侵犯的担忧。

• **情绪与呼吸的关系**：[CrimsonCape] 从情绪和生理角度讨论了呼吸的变化，强调了压力和紧张对呼吸的影响，并提出通过调节呼吸来改善情绪状态的可能性。

补充讨论：
• **呼吸模式识别的实际应用**：[guzik] 质疑这种研究在实际应用中的价值，尤其是需要佩戴设备的情况下。而 [kylehotchkiss] 和 [thenewwazoo] 则讨论了这种技术在零售和安全监控中的潜在应用，如通过mmWave传感器识别个人。

• **技术局限与讽刺**：[b0a04gl] 指出了研究中高准确率的局限性，如排除REM阶段，并幽默地指出了潜在的技术问题，如因感冒或运动后被系统误识别。

争议焦点：呼吸模式识别技术在实际应用中的价值和隐私侵犯问题。一些人认为这项技术在健康监测和身份识别中有潜力，而另一些人则担心隐私风险和实际可行性。

Twitter

Every breath you take ... could add to a breathing pattern that is unique to you, a study finds.
Credit: Anusak Laowilas/NurPhoto via Getty
Like the
swirls in fingerprints
, a person’s breathing pattern might be unique to them — offering a way not only to identify individuals, but also to identify some of their physical and mental traits.
A team of researchers measured the breathing of 97 healthy people for 24 hours, and found that they could identify participants with relatively high accuracy from their breathing pattern alone. What’s more, they found that these patterns can be correlated with body-mass index (BMI) and signs of depression and anxiety.
“In a way, we’re reading the mind through the nose,” says co-author Noam Sobel, a neurobiologist at the Weizmann Institute of Science in Rehovot, Israel. “This could be a very powerful diagnostic tool.” The team published its study today in
Current Biology
1
.
Taking a breath
Breathing is deeply connected to the brain. Every inhalation and exhalation is coordinated to supply the oxygen needed for the brain to manage the body’s systems. Sobel and his team wondered: if every brain functions differently, shouldn’t every person’s breathing be unique, too?
To test this, the researchers developed a custom, wearable device that records airflow through each of a person’s nostrils. Mounted on the back of the neck, the device, which has tubes fitted under the nose, tracks people’s breathing during their everyday routines, both while they are awake and while they are asleep.
Researchers measured study participants’ breathing patterns over 24 hours, using a custom device that sits on the back of the neck.
Credit: Soroka
et al., Current Biology
To characterize a person’s breath pattern, the team extracted 24 parameters from the airflow data, including duration of inhalation and exhalation and airflow asymmetry between nostrils. They separated the periods when participants were awake and asleep, and trained a machine-learning algorithm with the data.
When 42 of the participants came back to the laboratory weeks, months and even two years later, to take part in another 24-hour measurement, the trained algorithm could identify them from their breath patterns. Data from periods when the participants were awake gave more accurate results than did those from sleeping periods, but when the researchers used a 100-parameter characterization of a full data set instead of one using 24 parameters, they could pick individuals out with 96.8% accuracy.
Given this success, Sobel and his colleagues began wondering whether they could learn more from the breath patterns.
Healthy breathing
The researchers collected data on the participants’ BMIs, and from questionnaires that assess levels of depression and anxiety. An analysis found correlations between this information and the breathing patterns, even though most participants had low-level scores on the questionnaires.
For instance, the breathing profiles during sleep of people with higher BMIs were different from those of people with lower BMIs. And those who scored higher on the questionnaires for anxiety or depression had distinct patterns in how they inhaled and exhaled.

data.title: KDE Plasma 6.4 Released
data.author: jlpcsl
data.article_summary: Plasma 6.4 提供了更流畅、友好和实用的桌面体验，在可访问性、颜色渲染、平板支持和窗口管理等方面都有改进。新版本允许为每个虚拟桌面选择不同的平铺布局，增强了 Spectacle 截图工具，并让 KRunner 支持颜色代码输入和预览。窗口管理方面，结合了虚拟桌面和可定制平铺功能，用户可以创建适合自己的布局。可访问性方面，支持键盘控制指针和触摸板手势缩放。视觉设计上，Breeze Dark 主题变得更暗以提升对比度，并优化了认证对话框和系统设置界面。通知系统新增速度图显示文件传输进度，并支持直接从通知安装更新，还引入了“勿扰模式”和麦克风静音提示。桌面小部件也有改进，应用启动器新增“新应用”标签，媒体播放器支持调整播放速度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：KDE Plasma 桌面环境的功能改进和用户体验

不同观点：
• [garciansmith] 认为文件管理器的默认行为（每次拖动文件时询问移动或复制）曾是他刚使用 KDE 时的唯一不适应之处。虽然他后来习惯了这种操作，甚至开始喜欢上它（可以通过按住 shift 或 control 键自动选择移动或复制），但他很高兴现在这个行为变得可配置了。

• [keb_] 分享了自己将工作电脑和个人电脑都切换到了 Fedora KDE，并且非常喜欢这一环境，认为比 GNOME 好得多。

• [Rooster61] 表示由于 Windows 10 即将停止支持，他最近开始尝试使用 KDE Plasma，并且发现如今的 KDE 比十多年前要流畅得多，这让他能够顺利过渡到全职使用 Linux 图形界面。

• [kylebenzle] 称赞 KDE 是唯一一个他见过的不断变得更好的软件项目，暗示其持续的改进和优化。

• [speckx] 则关注即将推出的 per-workspace 平铺选项，表示对此功能的期待。

• 用户对 KDE Plasma 的功能改进（如文件管理器行为的可配置性）表示欢迎。
• 不同用户对 KDE 和 GNOME 等其他桌面环境有不同的偏好和体验。
• KDE Plasma 的长期发展和用户体验改进得到了用户的肯定，特别是在从其他操作系统（如 Windows）过渡到 Linux 的过程中。
• 即将推出的新功能（如 per-workspace 平铺选项）引起了用户的期待和关注。

44297685.article_content:
Plasma 6.4
Welcome /home
A smoother, friendlier and more helpful desktop experience
Tuesday, 17 June 2025
A new version of Plasma is here, and it feels even more like
/home
, as it becomes smoother, friendlier and more helpful.
Plasma 6.4 improves on nearly every front, with progress being made in accessibility, color rendering, tablet support, window management, and more.
As this is going to be a long read, letâs get right into itâ¦
Highlights
More Flexible Tiling
Choose a different tile layout for each of your virtual desktops
New Spectacle
Spectacle gets an overhaul to make it even more awesome
KRunner Gets Color
Enter a color code in any notation and let KRunner show you what it looks like
Window Management
Plasma already offers
Virtual Desktops
to help organize your windows and activities; and customizable
Tiles
you can stick windows to so they donât overlap, allowing you to see everything important at a glance.
Plasma 6.4 combines these features by letting you choose a different configuration of tiles on each virtual desktop.
The video below shows the power of this feature: you can tile two windows on your main virtual desktop, each taking up half of the screen. Then in another virtual desktop, you can place tile apps: two on either side, and the other two floating in the middle.
This new feature lets you create any other kind of layout combination that best works for you.
Accessibility
Accessibility is a top priority for KDE. This work is endless, but we make improvements in every new Plasma release!
The Wayland session in Plasma 6.4 brings some new accessibility features: you can now move the pointer using your keyboardâs number pad keys, or use a three-finger touchpad pinch gesture to zoom in or out.
In addition, a great deal of subtle but important work has been done throughout Plasma to improve keyboard navigation, screen reader usability, and text readability.
UI & Visual Design
Straddling the boundary between accessibility and visual design, another way of making Plasma easier to use is by increasing the contrast between the foreground and background elements.
In that respect, weâve made our
Breeze Dark
theme a bit darker. This subtle change helps the text and user interface elements pop, making them easier to read and see.
Plasma 6.4 also darkens the background of the desktop or window when an authentication dialog shows up. This will help you locate and focus on the window asking for your password.
The energy page in the
Info Center
and the entirety of
KMenuEdit
(the app you can use to edit appsâ presentation and grouping in the launcher menu) have all had their looks overhauled to make them cleaner, clearer, and easier to use.
Speaking of settings, thereâs a brand-new
Animations
page in
System Settings
that groups all the settings for purely visual animated effects into one place, making it easier to find and configure them.
Plasma 6.4âs lock screen plays nicer with multiple-screen setups, too. The lock screenâs interactive elements will now only appear on the screen that has focus or the pointer on it. And when itâs time to input your password, the text entered into one password field is synced across all others, avoiding any errors that may cause passwords to be half-entered in a field on one screen, and then the rest in a different one on another screen.
Notifications
Notifications are how Plasma communicates whatâs going on within your system.
The file transfer notification now shows a speed graph, giving you a more visual idea of how fast the transfer is going, and how long it will take to complete.
When you get notified that updates are available, you can now install them directly from the notification.
When any applications are in full screen mode â like when youâre playing a game, working on a critical project, or watching a video â Plasma will enter
Do Not Disturb
mode and only show urgent notifications. When you exit full screen mode, youâll see a summary of any notifications you missed, and theyâll be right there in the
System Tray
for your perusal.
Have you ever found yourself talking during an online meeting, and no one can hear you because you forgot to unmute your microphone? No more! Now when an app tries to access the microphone and finds it muted, a notification will pop up.
Finally, notifications with interactive buttons will still show them in the history view.
Widgets
Widgets are the building blocks of Plasma: small programs that carry out specific tasks on your Plasma desktop. They can launch programs, track the weather, set alarms, or tell you when you have updates.
Among many other improvements, a new feature in the
Application Launcher
widget will place a green
New!
tag next to newly installed apps, so you can easily find where something you just installed lives in the menu. The tag disappears after 3 days, or after you run the app for the first time.
The

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：租车中的车联网功能及其相关问题，包括隐私、功能限制和用户体验。

不同观点：
• **jsumrall**：提到在美国和荷兰租用宝马时，车联网功能被禁止，认为是宝马和租车公司有意设置的限制，建议向租车公司报告问题。
• **dylan604**：怀疑租车公司在车辆准备过程中不会彻底清理前一个租客的数据，建议用户自己删除个人信息，不要依赖租车公司。
• **bayindirh**：租用标致汽车时，遇到“租赁模式”提示，警告数据共享问题，虽然觉得信息透明但选择不连接Apple CarPlay。
• **nunez**：指出租车公司通常不为车联网服务做设置，只有少数例外（如FordPass与Avis和Tesla与Hertz的合作），并在租车后手动删除账户。
• **drdunce**：批评当前产品中软件质量低劣的问题被消费者忽视，认为如果是机械问题就不会被容忍。
• **Neywiny**：在美国租车时发现车辆未重置，充满上一位租客的偏好设置，认为租车公司应设有租赁模式。
• **hchak**：对这种“技巧”表示欣赏和兴趣。
• **abcd_f**：强烈批评宝马的车联网系统，认为其UX设计糟糕，功能隐藏在在线ID后，且取消过程繁琐，建议远离宝马。
• **thatjoeoverthr**：分享在意大利租用宝马的糟糕体验，表示以后不会再租用或购买宝马。
• **rcx141**：提到在Sixt租用的宝马无法关闭车道偏离技术，导致驾驶体验不佳。
• **bryant**：指出Enterprise Holdings通过车队管理限制宝马的车联网功能，包括订阅服务。
• **icedchai**：对租车公司正确处理这类事情不抱期望。
• **hyllos**：询问哪个汽车品牌在客户体验方面做得好。
• **bastawhiz**：提到从Carvana购买的特斯拉仍链接着前车主的账户信息，认为这是糟糕的客户服务。
• **7bit**：建议报告数据保护法（DPA）违规行为，租车公司有责任确保下一位租客的隐私。

补充讨论：
• **隐私问题**：多个评论提到租车公司未能有效清理前一个用户的数据，用户担心个人信息泄露。
• **功能受限**：宝马等租车公司对车联网功能的限制引发了用户的不满，尤其是当用户希望使用如Apple CarPlay等功能时。
• **用户体验**：用户普遍对宝马的复杂操作和不透明的功能设置感到不满，尤其是与在线ID相关的功能。
• **驾驶体验**：一些用户提到车联网功能中如车道偏离警告等技术在实际驾驶中造成不便。
• **责任归属**：有争议的焦点在于，租车公司是否应负责清理车辆数据以及设置租赁模式，还是用户应自行处理这些问题。

争议焦点：租车公司是否有责任确保车辆在租赁前被重置以及保障用户的隐私。

主要讨论点：微型电机的发展历史及其应用

不同观点：
• [kens] 回顾了微型电机发展的历史背景，提到了费曼在1959年的演讲《底部仍有很大空间》，该演讲被视为纳米技术领域的开端。kens强调，虽然有人很快赢得了费曼的电机挑战奖，但这个电机并没有应用任何新技术或推动纳米科技的进展。此外，kens还提到了1985年另一个与缩小文本相关的挑战成功完成，这标志着技术进步。

• [chaosprint] 对微型电机在实际产品中的应用表示关注，特别是提到了智能旋钮类产品，并询问是否存在可大规模生产、适用于此类产品的较大微型电机。这显示出对微型电机商业化应用的兴趣和需求。

• [blutack] 补充了关于手动浓缩咖啡机的例子，提到某公司曾生产过类似产品，但不确定在Kickstarter众筹活动后是否继续生产。这展示了微型电机在消费产品中的实际应用案例，并暗示了这类技术在市场中的生命周期可能较短。

补充讨论：
• 费曼的挑战和微型电机历史引发了对技术进步和实际应用之间的差距的讨论。kens指出，尽管早期微型电机赢得了奖金，但并没有显著推动纳米技术的发展。
• chaosprint和blutack的评论则更关注微型电机在消费电子和家用产品中的实际应用，反映了理论研究与市场产品化之间的联系与差距。

data.title: The Collapse of Complex Societies
data.author: giraffe_lady
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了对所谓“AI末日论”的批评，并指出这种担忧其实源于几十年前就存在的技术末日论传统。文章回顾了1972年出版的《增长的极限》一书，该书通过模型预测，若全球人口、工业化、污染、粮食生产和资源消耗等五大因素不加改变，地球将在未来一百年内达到增长极限，导致人口和工业能力急剧下降。该书的预测方法和结论曾引发争议，后续更新研究仍得出类似结果。

文章还介绍了1988年约瑟夫·泰恩特所著《复杂社会的崩溃》一书，泰恩特认为社会复杂性的增加会导致边际回报递减，最终复杂社会将因维持现状的成本过高而崩溃。这与《增长的极限》的预测相呼应，提出了当前社会是否正在接近崩溃的问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社会崩溃的可能性及其预测模型的有效性

不同观点：
• **myflash13** 认为社会不一定因为某个节点而彻底结束，但生活质量会持续恶化，尤其是在西方国家。他以千禧一代的经济状况为例，指出大多数人生活状况不如父母，只有少数移居其他地区的人例外。

• **gweinberg** 对预测社会崩溃的模型持怀疑态度。他认为这些模型虽然看似 robust（坚固），但其基本假设存在高度可疑之处，因为无论如何调整参数，最终都会得出崩溃的结论，只是时间问题。

• **Isamu** 指出，批评“AI 末日论者”的人往往忽视了技术末日论有着几十年的知识传统。他质疑像《增长的极限》这类模型中的数学假设，认为其曲线选择是随意的，缺乏实证依据。此外，他认为“崩溃”一词被广泛滥用，导致讨论变得模糊和夸张。

• **gmuslera** 用“囚徒困境”类比全球社会动态，指出所有参与者都朝着墙加速前进，任何一方试图减速都会被其他方损害。因此，在这种系统中，重新定义“理性行动”变得至关重要。

• **vdupras** 提出，人类社会依赖于复杂的承诺网络。这些承诺层层叠加，互相利用。未来的承诺已经被大量预支，任何试图解决这些承诺的人都会发现大规模的承诺破灭不可避免，这将导致社会资源缩减、冲突增加，最终可能引发崩溃。

补充讨论：
- 对“崩溃”一词的定义和使用存在争议，Isamu 认为其过于模糊和夸张，影响了理性讨论。
- 模型的基本假设和预测的有效性是争议焦点，gweinberg 和 Isamu 都对其持怀疑态度。
- 讨论中涉及了系统动态、囚徒困境等复杂系统理论，表明社会崩溃可能不仅仅是经济问题，还涉及社会结构和决策理性。

Those who critÂ­iÂ­cize so-called

ex nihilo
vs. a reasoned arguÂ­ment that it necesÂ­sarily emerges from specific human deciÂ­sions and
habits.
The Limits of Growth
This book, published in 1972, was an early effort to quanÂ­tiÂ­taÂ­tively model the effects of techÂ­noÂ­logÂ­ical change. I read it some years ago. As the title implies,
The Limits of Growth

five key global factors

If the present growth trends in world popuÂ­laÂ­tion, indusÂ­triÂ­alÂ­izaÂ­tion, polluÂ­tion, food producÂ­tion, and resource depleÂ­tion continue unchanged, the limits to growth on this planet will be reached someÂ­time within the next one hundred years. The most probÂ­able result will be a rather
sudden and unconÂ­trolÂ­lable decline in both popuÂ­laÂ­tion and indusÂ­trial capacity
.
In support of their theoÂ­ries, and unusuÂ­ally for the era, the authors of TLoG relied extenÂ­sively on softÂ­ware simuÂ­laÂ­tions. This allowed the authors to, say, model the course of human progress under realÂ­istic current assumpÂ­tions. In this model, popuÂ­laÂ­tion decreases rapidly after aroundÂ

sooner
because unconÂ­trolled polluÂ­tion negates the beneÂ­fits of the extra

For 1972, these charts are pretty rad. They remind me of output from programs in my beloved childÂ­hood copy of

RecalÂ­iÂ­braÂ­tion of Limits to Growth
, a sepaÂ­rate group of authors ran the TLoG simuÂ­laÂ­tions with updated empirÂ­ical data. Result? You guessedÂ

44300027.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了对所谓“AI末日论”的批评，并指出这种担忧其实源于几十年前就存在的技术末日论传统。文章回顾了1972年出版的《增长的极限》一书，该书通过模型预测，若全球人口、工业化、污染、粮食生产和资源消耗等五大因素不加改变，地球将在未来一百年内达到增长极限，导致人口和工业能力急剧下降。该书的预测方法和结论曾引发争议，后续更新研究仍得出类似结果。

文章还介绍了1988年约瑟夫·泰恩特所著《复杂社会的崩溃》一书，泰恩特认为社会复杂性的增加会导致边际回报递减，最终复杂社会将因维持现状的成本过高而崩溃。这与《增长的极限》的预测相呼应，提出了当前社会是否正在接近崩溃的问题。
44300027.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社会崩溃的可能性及其预测模型的有效性

不同观点：
• **myflash13** 认为社会不一定因为某个节点而彻底结束，但生活质量会持续恶化，尤其是在西方国家。他以千禧一代的经济状况为例，指出大多数人生活状况不如父母，只有少数移居其他地区的人例外。

• **gweinberg** 对预测社会崩溃的模型持怀疑态度。他认为这些模型虽然看似 robust（坚固），但其基本假设存在高度可疑之处，因为无论如何调整参数，最终都会得出崩溃的结论，只是时间问题。

• **Isamu** 指出，批评“AI 末日论者”的人往往忽视了技术末日论有着几十年的知识传统。他质疑像《增长的极限》这类模型中的数学假设，认为其曲线选择是随意的，缺乏实证依据。此外，他认为“崩溃”一词被广泛滥用，导致讨论变得模糊和夸张。

• **gmuslera** 用“囚徒困境”类比全球社会动态，指出所有参与者都朝着墙加速前进，任何一方试图减速都会被其他方损害。因此，在这种系统中，重新定义“理性行动”变得至关重要。

• **vdupras** 提出，人类社会依赖于复杂的承诺网络。这些承诺层层叠加，互相利用。未来的承诺已经被大量预支，任何试图解决这些承诺的人都会发现大规模的承诺破灭不可避免，这将导致社会资源缩减、冲突增加，最终可能引发崩溃。

补充讨论：
- 对“崩溃”一词的定义和使用存在争议，Isamu 认为其过于模糊和夸张，影响了理性讨论。
- 模型的基本假设和预测的有效性是争议焦点，gweinberg 和 Isamu 都对其持怀疑态度。
- 讨论中涉及了系统动态、囚徒困境等复杂系统理论，表明社会崩溃可能不仅仅是经济问题，还涉及社会结构和决策理性。

data.title: Rules, Not Renewables, Might Explain the Iberian Blackout
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了2021年发生在伊比利亚半岛的大规模停电事件，指出停电原因可能并非可再生能源问题，而是电网管理规则不足。作者认为，未来的电网需要更好地激励和管理无功功率，以维持电力系统的稳定性。无功功率在电压控制中起关键作用，而当前的规则和激励措施可能不足以应对可再生能源接入带来的挑战。文章强调，改进电网管理和规则制定比单纯增加可再生能源容量更为重要，以防止类似停电事件再次发生。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：可再生能源在电网中的技术问题及责任归属

不同观点：
• **cogman10的观点**：可再生能源在电网中的“孤岛化”问题（renewable islanding）是一个技术问题，而不是规则问题。可再生能源不愿成为无功功率源，当频率下降时，它们往往会切断电源以避免对电网和其他电力供应商造成损害。相比之下，传统的旋转圆盘电源供应商具有动量，能够承受低电压并自我纠正，而可再生能源缺乏这种能力。因此，解决办法是制定针对可再生能源生产者的规则，要求安装必要的孤岛设备，而不是简单地切断电源。

• **diggan的观点**：目前关于电网故障原因的讨论为时尚早。引用了西班牙电网运营商REE误算导致大规模停电的事件，并指出官方调查尚未得出结论，预计需要数月时间才能发布报告。diggan认为在官方结论发布之前，进行原因猜测和争论没有太大意义。

• **ErneX的观点**：指出能源结构已经发生变化，增加了更多联合循环发电（combined cycle），这可能暗示了问题的根源所在，即能源结构的变化可能影响了电网的稳定性。

• **MaxHoppersGhost的观点**：认为欧洲调查者不可能将责任归咎于可再生能源，暗示可能存在对可再生能源的偏见或保护。

补充讨论：
• **jakub_g的观点**：提到相关的平行讨论，即西班牙电网运营商的误算导致了大规模停电，进一步指出在缺乏官方结论的情况下进行猜测和讨论可能不准确。
• 争议焦点在于可再生能源在电网故障中的责任问题，一部分人认为技术问题是主要原因，而另一部分人则认为在官方调查结果发布前进行猜测没有意义，还有人暗示对可再生能源的偏见。

data.title: What I Wish Someone Told Me When I Was Getting into ARIA
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了ARIA（可访问富互联网应用程序）的概念及其在网页可访问性中的作用。ARIA为HTML标记提供额外信息，帮助屏幕阅读器和语音控制软件更好地理解网页内容。它用于描述交互性、目的和状态，例如按钮是否被激活或折叠面板的当前状态。ARIA并非一本如何构建无障碍网站的指南，而是帮助设计和开发人员正确理解和使用ARIA的思维框架。文章还回顾了ARIA的历史和发展，指出其初版发布于2006年，最新版为2023年的1.2版本，并简要提及了其未来发展。作者强调，ARIA是HTML局限性的补充，使用时需谨慎，以避免误用带来的问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ARIA（可访问富互联网应用程序）在实现自定义元素无障碍设计中的作用和效果

不同观点：
• **[rhdunn] 支持使用 ARIA 作者实践指南 (APG)**：rhdunn 认为 ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG) 是其实现自定义元素时的重要参考，因为该指南清晰规定了给定元素在特定状态下的键盘导航、ARIA 角色、状态和属性的要求，比直接阅读核心规范更易于实施和测试。

• **[askew] 强调谨慎使用 ARIA，避免滥用**：askew 同意 ARIA 可以在将不规范的 "div 汤"（指 HTML 结构混乱的页面）转化为更具可访问性的元素方面发挥重要作用，但指出像文章中提到的，随意使用 `aria-label` 并不会自动使界面可访问，反而可能带来意外的负面效果。

• **[nailer] 认为 ARIA 是“釜底抽薪”式的解决方案，主张通过计算机视觉模型替代**：nailer 认为 ARIA 只是帮助了无障碍行业，但并不是解决问题的最佳方式。他提出，更好的解决方案是通过专注于无障碍的计算机视觉模型来解决可访问性问题。

补充讨论：
• **ARIA 的有效性和使用限制**：评论中讨论了 ARIA 的优势和潜在问题，特别是如果使用不当（如滥用 `aria-label`），可能会产生负面影响。
• **技术替代方案的讨论**：nailer 提出了使用计算机视觉模型作为 ARIA 的替代方案，这引出了关于未来无障碍技术发展方向的讨论。
• **争议焦点**：ARIA 是否是解决可访问性问题的最佳工具，尤其是在有其他技术（如计算机视觉模型）可以选择的情况下。

Accessible Rich Internet Applications (ARIA)
is an inevitability when working on web accessibility. That said, it’s everyone’s first time learning about ARIA at some point.
If you haven’t encountered ARIA before, great! It’s a chance to learn something new and exciting. If you have heard of ARIA before, this might help you better understand it or maybe even teach you something new!
These are all things I wish someone had told me when I was getting started on my web accessibility journey. This post will:
Provide a mindset for
how to approach ARIA
as a concept,
Debunk some common misconceptions
, and
Provide some guiding thoughts
to help you better understand and work with it.
It is my hope that in doing so, this post will help make an oft-overlooked yet vital corner of web design and development easier to approach.
What This Post Is Not
This
is not
a recipe book for how to use ARIA to build accessible websites and web apps. It is also not a guide for how to remediate an inaccessible experience.
A lot of accessibility work is highly contextual
. I do not know the specific needs of your project or organization, so trying to give advice here could easily do more harm than good.
Instead, think of this post as a “know before you go” guide. I’m hoping to give you a good headspace to approach ARIA, as well as highlight things to watch out for when you undertake your journey. So, with that out of the way, let’s dive in!
Roll up your sleeves and
boost your UX skills
! Meet
Smart Interface Design Patterns
🍣, a 10h video library by Vitaly Friedman.
100s of real-life examples
and live UX training.
Free preview
.
Jump to table of contents ↬
So, What Is ARIA?
ARIA is what you turn to if there is not a native HTML element or attribute that is better suited for the job of communicating interactivity, purpose, and state.
Think of it like a spice that you sprinkle into your markup to enhance things.
Adding ARIA to your HTML markup is a way of providing additional information to a website or web app for
screen readers
and
voice control software
.
Interactivity
means the content can be activated or manipulated. An example of this is navigating to a link’s destination.
Purpose
means what something is used for. An example of this is a text input used to collect someone’s name.
State
means the current status content has been placed in and controlled by
states, properties, and values
. An example of this is an accordion panel ​​that can either be expanded or collapsed.
Here is an illustration to help communicate what I mean by this:
(
Large preview
)
The presence of
HTML’s
button
element
will instruct assistive technology to report it as a button, letting someone know that it can be activated to perform a predefined action.
The presence of the text string “Mute” will be reported by assistive technology to clue the person into what the button is used for.
The presence of
aria-pressed="true"
means that someone or something has previously activated the button, and it is now in a “pushed in” state that sustains its action.
This overall pattern will let people who use assistive technology know:
If something is interactive,
What kind of interactive behavior it performs, and
Its
current state
.
ARIA’s History
ARIA has been around for a long time, with
the first version published on September 26th, 2006
.
(
Large preview
)
ARIA was created to provide a bridge between the limitations of HTML and the need for making interactive experiences understandable by assistive technology.
“
The latest version of ARIA is
version 1.2
, published on June 6th, 2023. Version 1.3 is slated to be released relatively soon, and you can read more about it in
this excellent article by Craig Abbott
.
You may also see it referred to as WAI-ARIA, where WAI stands for “Web Accessibility Initiative.” The
WAI
is part of the
W3C
, the organization that sets standards for the web. That said, most accessibility practitioners I know call it “ARIA” in written and verbal communication and leave out the “WAI-” part.
The Spirit Of ARIA Reflects The Era In Which It Was Created
The reason for this is simple: The web was a lot less mature in the past than it is now. The most popular operating system in 2006 was
Windows XP
. The iPhone didn’t exist yet; it was released a year later.
From a very high level,
ARIA is a snapshot of the operating system interaction paradigms of this time period

data.title: How the little-known 'dark roof' lobby may be making US cities hotter
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 2010年8月19日，志愿者在纽约布朗克斯为一个屋顶涂上具有高太阳反射率和红外发射率的特殊涂料。这种反光屋顶可以降低城市温度并节省能源，但暗色屋顶制造商正悄然游说阻止相关新规。2025年，田纳西州废除商用建筑必须使用反光屋顶的规定，共和党议员Rusty Grills称此举是为增加消费者选择。批评者警告，这将导致更高的能源成本和更多的热相关疾病。科学表明，浅色屋顶在炎热天气下温度比深色屋顶低50度以上，有助于减少能源使用和温室气体排放。至少八个州和十几个城市已采用反光屋顶要求，但行业团体质疑其科学依据，并反对全国统一标准。随着全球变暖，屋顶已成为气候战争的关键战场。

主要讨论点：城市规划中的热上升气流及其环境影响，特别是对不同区域和人群的影响是否公平。

不同观点：
• 观点一：有人（如squircle）认为，虽然强热上升气流本身可能没有错，但需要证明这种由市场驱动的、自上而下的城市规划方式不会将熵（即无序和环境负担）转嫁给其他人或地区。评论者质疑当前的规划方式是否忽视了我们彼此之间的相互联系，以及这种规划对不同人群的影响是否公平。他们特别提到，不应让某些群体（如其他人的孩子）承受环境负担，而自己却置身事外。

• 观点二：隐含的对立观点可能是默认当前的城市规划和市场驱动的方式是可接受的，且没有显著的环境不公问题。虽然没有明确表述，但从squircle的评论中可以看出，他们反对这种立场，认为有必要质疑和检验当前的做法是否在环境和社会责任方面存在问题。

补充讨论：
• Squircle通过对比在阴凉公园和沥青停车场中的温度差异，指出了不同城市区域的热环境差异，这可能是由城市设计和材料选择导致的。评论者质疑是否有人研究并证明了这种设计不会对环境或某些群体造成不公。

• 评论还提到了生物区域主义（bioregional sense）的概念，这表明在城市规划中应更多考虑环境和生态因素，并质疑当前以市场为主导的规划是否忽视了这些因素。

争议焦点：当前市场驱动的城市规划是否在无形中加剧了环境不公，将某些负面影响（如热上升气流和环境负担）转嫁给特定区域或弱势群体，而受益者却不必承担相应后果。这涉及到环境正义和城市设计中的公平性问题。

Photograph: Ken Cavanagh/Alamy
View image in fullscreen
