data.title: Occurences of swearing in the Linux kernel source code over time
data.author: microsoftedging
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了在一个交互式网页工具中搜索Linux内核源代码中特定词汇、名称或函数出现次数的方法。用户可以输入以逗号分隔的关键词列表进行查询，支持使用通配符`*`和逻辑或`foo|bar`进行组合搜索。如果启用Javascript，用户可以看到交互式图形；否则只能查看过时的静态图片。文章还提供了单词匹配的规则，并邀请用户探索作者的其他有趣项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源代码中使用的语言，包括咒骂词、技术术语以及其背后的文化和社会影响

不同观点：
• PaulHoule和sschueller指出，"retarded" 可以是一个技术术语，意为“延迟”，而非侮辱性词语。PaulHoule还通过法语和英语中的例子（如"Couche-Tard"和"L'Ensemble Quotodienne"）说明了语言间的趣味差异。
• holowoodman认为，咒骂词的减少是企业化（corporatization）的结果，使得代码变得乏味、缺乏个性。
• Pannoniae认为，咒骂词的存在意味着开发者更有激情，而不是为了简历或企业目的而编写代码。同时，这也能筛选出那些容易被触发不满的人。
• d3m0t3p关注公司对开源项目的贡献，通过数据展示Google、Apple、Meta和IBM的贡献变化，质疑这些公司对项目的实际影响。
• gwbas1c分享了一个实习经历，提到在源代码中搜索咒骂词以区分专业与非专业行为，并举例说明了搜索“moron”的结果。
• lloydatkinson担心记录这些语言现象会导致进一步的政治化和敌意，并提到了将代码分支从"master"改名为"main"的例子。
• b0a04gl对数据分析的深度提出质疑，认为仅通过grep图表无法展示公司对代码的结构性影响。
• bArray指出某些词语如"ass"和"dumb"在图表中的使用频率增加，并提供了相关链接以支持其观点。
• tianqi对"garbage"等词语的使用增长表示兴趣，并询问这是否反映了英语的演变。
• egypturnash通过引用图表数据，幽默地提到“Linus说同性恋权利”。
• dhsysusbsjsi作为澳大利亚人，对图表中缺乏"cunt"一词表示失望。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是咒骂词在代码中的存在是否代表了开发者的激情和个性，还是缺乏专业性。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是公司对开源项目的实际贡献，以及如何通过数据分析来评估这些贡献。
• 语言和文化的差异在讨论中也扮演了重要角色，例如法语和英语之间的趣味差异。
• 政治化问题也被提及，特别是在技术领域中对语言和术语的选择和更改。

data.title: High levels of antihistamine drugs can reduce fitness gains
data.author: bikenaga
data.article_summary: 一项由俄勒冈大学进行的研究发现，高剂量的抗组胺药物会干扰有氧运动中的健身收益。组胺这种分子不仅与过敏反应有关，还在运动表现和恢复中起重要作用。研究比较了两组参与为期六周骑行训练的受试者，一组服用抗组胺药物，另一组服用安慰剂。结果显示，抗组胺药物组的有氧健身改善减少了一半，血流量增加也显著低于安慰剂组。尽管最大摄氧量（VO2 max）的改善没有明显差异，但阻断组胺影响了约四分之一与肌肉恢复相关基因的表达，导致肌肉产生的蛋白质减少，从而影响健身收益。研究表明，抗组胺药物可能削弱运动带来的健身提升，尤其是有氧运动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：抗组胺药物（抗过敏药物）对运动表现和生理功能的潜在影响

不同观点：
• [username44] 分享了个人经历，表明在服用抗组胺药物（famotidine和fexofenadine）期间，日常跑步变得更为困难，停止用药后情况改善。这暗示抗组胺药物可能对运动表现有负面影响。

• [AnthonBerg] 从生理学角度分析，指出组胺在警觉性和代谢中的作用，特别是与葡萄糖代谢的关联。他将组胺视为一种“组织开启信号”，认为抗组胺药物可能通过干扰这一机制影响身体表现。

• [jameskilton] 提到当前研究中使用的高剂量抗组胺药物远超一般抗过敏用途的剂量，因此质疑这些研究结果是否能直接应用于日常低剂量服用抗过敏药的人群。他认为需要更多证据来确定低剂量抗组胺药物是否会影响健身表现。

• [UK-AL] 简要提及个人因严重花粉过敏而长期服用抗组胺药物，未讨论药物对运动的影响，但暗示这些药物对其过敏症状是必要的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于抗组胺药物对运动表现的影响是否与剂量有关。高剂量药物的影响已被研究证实，但低剂量用于过敏治疗时的影响尚不明确，需要更多研究支持。

• 组胺作为一种多功能神经递质，其在警觉性和代谢中的角色被[AnthonBerg]强调，这为理解抗组胺药物的广泛影响提供了新的视角。

• 个人经历和科学研究之间的差异也被提及，[username44]的个人经验和[jameskilton]对研究细节的关注形成了对比。

Credit:
Journal of Applied Physiology
(2025). DOI: 10.1152/japplphysiol.00687.2024
For some, the word "histamine" might evoke thoughts of seasonal allergies: runny noses, scratchy throats and itchy eyes. But the molecule also influences exercise performance.
A new study from the University of Oregon underscores its beneficial role in aerobic activity and exercise recovery, showing that blocking
histamine
at high levels interferes with fitness gains. It remains to be seen if lower-dose, over-the-counter antihistamine drugs have the same effect.
The study was published in the
Journal of Applied Physiology
.
Histamine is a small signaling molecule that evolved long ago. It is found in many plants and animals, including single-celled organisms, which use it to signal and adapt to stress.
"In exercise, it actually seems to be playing a very similar role of facilitating our adaptation to stress," said John Halliwill, a professor of human physiology at the University of Oregon and an author on the study.
In humans, histamine is part of the immune system; it passes along the message that inflammation is needed somewhere. During allergy season, for example, pollen triggers the release of histamine from mast cells, an immune system component.
Then, an
inflammatory response
floods the area to try and get rid of the pollen, causing typical seasonal allergy symptoms. That's why drugs known as antihistamines, such as Claritin and Zyrtec, are used to treat seasonal allergies.
Inflammation is also linked to fitness improvements because muscles are microscopically damaged during exercise and need to be repaired, which also builds new muscle tissue. Halliwill and colleagues found that when histamine is blocked, aerobic fitness improvements were slashed in half.
The team compared the improvements in a group of 16 men and women participating in a six-week cycling regimen. Participants pedaled on stationary bikes three to four times a week over the course of the study. One group received a dose of antihistamine medication before each training session while the other group took a placebo. Then, researchers compared how the groups' bodies adapted.
When it came to their actual performance—how hard they could bike—the
placebo group
saw about twice the improvement of the histamine-blocker group. Improvements in blood flow were also significantly higher in the placebo group, the team reported.
Interestingly, there wasn't a strong difference between the groups' improvements in maximum oxygen consumption. Often called VO
2
max in the fitness world, it's the maximum amount of oxygen the body can absorb and use, with a higher VO
2
max signaling better fitness.
It could be the study size was too small to see a difference, or six weeks might not have been long enough to uncover a change between the groups, Halliwill said.
Scientists first suspected that histamine might be a part of the body's response to exercise in the 1970s. The idea didn't gain traction until the last decade or so, with researchers now trying to tease apart the relationship.
Just like an allergic reaction, it starts with mast cells, which are found throughout
skeletal muscle tissue
. When those muscles are working, they trigger the
mast cells
to spill their histamine, although researchers aren't yet sure what spurs that reaction.
The histamine causes
blood vessels
to dilate, allowing more
blood flow
to the muscles. When the muscle goes back to resting, the histamine continues to have an effect by prompting a cascade of immune responses, which brings beneficial inflammation to the area.
"We've got a whole village of cell types that are turning on programs to remodel and restructure and improve the function of the skeletal muscle-organ system," Halliwill said. "Mast cells and the histamine that they release are a major coordinator of all those cell types."
Histamine also seems to boost the response of certain genes during exercise. When histamine is blocked, about a quarter of those 3,000 or so genes aren't amplified. That means fewer new proteins get produced by muscles as they recover from exercise, and those proteins likely play key roles in fitness gains, like the ones measured in the UO study.
Before Halliwill's paper came out, a different group published a similar study looking at the effect of antihistamines during high-intensity interval training. Halliwill said both studies' results are in agreement that blocking histamine reduced a person's fitness gains. The results could apply to any form of aerobic activity, be it

data.title: Photon transport through the entire adult human head
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了光子穿过成年人整个头部的极限传输能力，特别关注在光源和探测器位于头部两侧的极端情况下，光子如何在脑内迁移。研究结合了数值模拟和时间分辨光子计数实验，测量脉冲光通过头部的传输情况。结果显示，实验与模拟在峰值延迟时间和相关直方图宽度上高度一致，光子迁移路径分析表明，该方法对大脑区域的敏感性远超现有非侵入式光学成像的限制。研究成功检测到衰减约10¹⁸的光子，并发现通过调整光源位置可以针对大脑特定区域（如小脑深部）进行成像。该研究为非侵入式光学脑成像技术提供了新的可能性，特别是对深层脑区成像的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新型近红外光技术在脑成像中的应用及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• **freehorse**：  
  - 认为该技术基于现有的功能性近红外光谱技术（fNIRS），但试图通过增加光源和检测器的距离来探测更深层的脑组织。
  - 提出该实验在受控条件下完成（浅肤色、无头发、记录时间短），其实际应用尚不明确。
  - 对该技术能否像现有的fNIRS或fMRI一样有效测量脑活动持怀疑态度，认为信号可能过于嘈杂且不具备高空间特异性。
  - 同时指出，尽管目前应用前景不明，但可能带来无法预见的创新。

• **rkagerer**：  
  - 引用论文内容，指出该技术探测的脑区是当前非侵入性光学成像无法触及的区域。
  - 强调该技术在探索新领域方面的潜力。

• **xnx**：  
  - 询问该技术是否可用于其他组织，或是否已经在其他领域得到应用。
  - 对光穿透身体组织的广泛应用表示好奇。

• **antiquark**：  
  - 关注信号的强度问题，指出实验中检测到的光子数量极少（每秒约一个光子），对实际应用中的信号质量表示担忧。

• **ggm**：  
  - 比较该技术与X射线或核磁共振成像（MRI）的风险和成像质量。
  - 质疑该技术是否能在提供相似成像质量的同时降低风险。

• **aetherspawn**：  
  - 误解标题，以为研究涉及光子“瞬间传送”穿过头部，反映出对技术实现的误解或期望过高。

• **ars**：  
  - 质疑如何从光子模式中获取深度信息，认为通过测量信号往返时间（飞行时间）可能更有效。
  - 同时提出该技术目前仅适用于浅肤色患者，若临床应用可能引发争议。

补充讨论：
- 该技术是否能在非侵入性脑成像中提供新的突破，尤其是在探测深度和空间特异性方面。
- 信号强度和深度信息的获取是主要技术挑战。
- 临床应用的潜力和限制，尤其是在不同肤色人群中的适用性问题，可能引发伦理争议。

争议焦点：
- 该技术能否真正应用于脑活动测量，以及在不同人群中的公平使用问题。

Abstract
Significance
The highly scattering nature of near-infrared light in human tissue makes it challenging to collect photons using source-detector separations larger than several centimeters. The limits of detectability of light transmitted through the head remain unknown. Detecting photons in the extreme case through an entire adult head explores the limits of photon transport in the brain.
Aim
We explore the physical limits of photon transport in the head in the extreme case wherein the source and detector are diametrically opposite.
Approach
Simulations uncover possible migration pathways of photons from source to detector. We compare simulations with time-resolved photon counting experiments that measure pulsed light transmitted through the head.
Results
We observe good agreement between the peak delay time and width of the time-correlated histograms in experiments and simulations. Analysis of the photon migration pathways indicates sensitivity to regions of the brain well beyond accepted limits. Source repositioning can isolate sensitivity to targeted regions of the brain, including under the cerebrum.
Conclusions
We overcome attenuation of
∼
10
18
and detect photons transmitted through an entire adult human head for a subject with fair skin and no hair. Photons measured in this regime explore regions of the brain currently inaccessible with noninvasive optical brain imaging.
1.
Introduction
Optical modalities for noninvasive imaging of the human brain hold promise to fill the technology gap between cheap and portable devices such as electroencephalography (EEG) and expensive high-resolution instruments such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), with devices that have high sample rates, high spatial resolution, and are relatively inexpensive. A major bottleneck for the widespread adoption of optical brain reading devices in clinics and neuroscience studies is the low number of photons emerging from deep layers of the brain that restrict the sensitivity of these methods to a maximum of 4 cm below the scalp,
